articles.title: Jack Singleton joins Glasgow Warriors a year after cardiac event
articles.summary: Former England hooker Jack Singleton joins Glasgow Warriors on a short-term deal a year after experiencing a cardiac event in training.
articles.body:
Former England hooker Jack Singleton has joined Glasgow Warriors 13 months after experiencing a cardiac event in training.

The 30-year-old has agreed a short-term deal to provide cover during the Nations Championship and Six Nations.

Singleton spent six years with Gloucester, where he scored 20 tries in 75 appearances, after playing for Worcester and Saracens.

He admits the thought of never playing again "definitely crossed my mind" as he had stents and balloons fitted to open up his arteries.

"It's a hereditary condition that we didn't know about," he explained. "Since the operations and procedures that I've had and the drugs that I'm now taking, everything's more under control.

"I'm in a much safer spot than I was 16 months ago when I was playing."

Singleton, who has four England caps, has been doing "full running sessions" since May but is unsure of when he will be fit to resume playing.

"I'm looking forward to just getting stuck into training," he said. "It's a massive privilege for me to be a part of this group.

"I've seen the success in the European runs they went on last year. I remember watching that Toulouse game and the atmosphere looked unbelievable.

"Honestly, if they asked me to play this weekend, I'd get out there. I probably wouldn't give a great account of myself, to be fair."

Singleton last represented England in 2022 and is Scottish-qualified through his grandparents.

However, he is not looking beyond getting back on the pitch with the Warriors.

"I'm more just worrying about training right now and then hopefully playing, and then we'll see what happens after," he said.

Glasgow hookers Gregor Hiddleston and Seb Stephen are likely to be called up for Scotland's internationals in November, February and March.

articles.title: Stupaczuk se reinventa y ya llama a la puerta del 'Club de los Diez'
articles.standfirst: El argentino, que debutó en 2014, se mantiene vigente tras su primer gran título en 2016 convirtiéndose en uno de los jugadores más regulares de la historia moderna.
articles.summary: El argentino, que debutó en la élite en 2014, se mantiene vigente tras su primer gran título en 2016 convirtiéndose en uno de los jugadores más regulares de la historia moderna.
articles.body: ¿Tiene el selecto ‘Club de los Diez’ nuevo miembro? A este distinguido grupo que reúne a los jugadores que han sido capaces de, al menos, ganar un trofeo por año 10 temporadas consecutivas aspira Franco Stupaczuk en su décima temporada completa en la élite del pádel y que le sitúa a la altura de unos pocos elegidos como Fernando Belasteguín, Juan Martín Díaz, Pablo Lima, Sanyo Gutiérrez o Paquito Navarro. Hay que remontarse muchos años atrás para hablar de la irrupción del ‘Polaco’. Cuando su casi impronunciable apellido era desconocido, el primer seudónimo que se asoció a su nombre fue el de ‘Los Superpibes’. La irrupción junto a un también joven Martín Di Nenno alteró el pádel profesional cuando en 2013 ganaron el Mundial, debutaron un año después en World Padel Tour y ya en 2015 lograron su primer título con el Barcelona Challenger. Por aquel entonces el pádel era un deporte de nicho que se miraba con asombro en sus primeras emisiones en la televisión en abierto. Unos años en los que Bela y Lima eran tan imbatibles que se tuvo que cambiar la pelota a una más viva y en los que tan solo había tres torneos al año fuera de España. En ese contexto, por la desgracia ya conocida de su compañero, Franco empezaría su carrera en solitario. Era 2016 y un joven Stupa compartiría primer proyecto y aprendizaje junto al brasileño Marcello Jardim, un veterano de mil batallas, con el que dejaría para el recuerdo aquella actuación en La Rural de Buenos Aires donde el zénit de los cuartos de final ante la pareja tres le valió el emblemático cántico de la grada de "Olé, olé, olé, olé, Franco, Franco". Un año en el que llegaría también su segundo título Challenger, este junto a Fede Quiles en la Costa del Sol y se alzaría con el título de Jugador Revelación en los prestigiosos PadelSpain World Padel Awards. Un 2016 que le valdría para ponerse en el escaparate por su juego eléctrico, ágil, vistoso y de determinante remate en suspensión, que le haría dar el salto cualitativo de la mano de Cristian Gutiérrez. Con ‘El Gordo’ (apodo cariñoso con el que se conoce al genio de Mar del Plata), llegaría el primer título. En julio de 2017 y a los 21 años Stupa se coronaría por primera vez en la élite y por partida doble y consecutiva. Los Open de Mijas y Gran Canaria le verían asaltar la victoria junto a Gutiérrez y aunque no llegarían más aquel año, pisaría varias finales para volver a tocar el éxito ya entrado el 2018 con el Granada Open. Dos temporadas con Gutiérrez le valdrían para dar un nuevo salto en un proyecto junto a Mati Díaz. Un tándem que no acabaría de funcionar por las lesiones y recaídas de ambos durante todo el curso, pero que también vería campeonar a Franco con el ‘Warrior’ en el Córdoba Open y le haría estar entre los mejores. Así llegaría 2020, el año más sui generis de la historia moderna. Una temporada en la que afrontaría una prometedora unión con Sanyo Gutiérrez, el ex número uno. Partiendo como pareja 3 el argentino viviría un vía crucis personal quedando desdibujado y sometido a un exceso de presión externa e interna que sintetiza a la perfección aquel remate para ganar el partido en las semifinales de Marbella, el primer torneo de la temporada, y que quedaría en el limbo de la verja ante unos debutantes Galán y Lebrón que acabarían marcando una época. Una tibia temporada en la que también lograría la victoria en Menorca y que le llevaría tras varios años adoptando el rol de meritorio, de joven talento, a apostar por ser el líder de un proyecto. Entrando en la madurez deportiva con 24 años el discípulo de Carlos Pozzoni (no se puede entender su carrera sin el que ha sido su fiel entrenador y asesor) apostaría por el español Álex Ruiz para crecer y reclamar el foco. 2021 sería un año sobresaliente para una dupla que empezaría con la vitola de tapada y que acabaría el curso con dos campeonatos en Cagliari y Ciudad de México y hasta tres finales más para escalar a la cuarta plaza del ranking. Unos resultados exigentes y difíciles de igualar que acabarían por separar sus caminos iniciado el segundo trimestre de 2022 para que volara en busca de éxito junto una leyenda como Pablo Lima. Con el brasileño lastrado a causa de unos problemas de rodilla que arrastraba desde 2021, Stupa alcanzaría su mejor versión hasta el momento. Más hecho como jugador, con más recursos y una curva de aprendizaje notable en la gestión de los partidos y la toma de decisiones, tocarían la victoria por partida doble en la transición World Padel Tour y Premier Padel. Un campeonato en Francia más cuatro finales en el circuito de Damm y dos trofeos en Mendoza y Newgiza en el nuevo circuito catarí serían la cuenta final de un 2022 en el que, además, volvería a reavivar la llama de ‘Los Superpibes’ en el Mundial pasando por encima de la dupla española Coello y Galán en la final para forzar el tercer punto que haría campeona a Argentina. Así arrancó 2023, reavivando la llama donde hubo cenizas. El Mundial volvería a unir a Stupaczuk y Di Nenno en una versión 2.0 madura, hecha y con la ambición de asaltar el trono mundial que ilusionaba al deporte de la pala por la mística de su pasado. No lo conseguirían, cierto, pero su temporada sería para enmarcar con cinco títulos y siete finales entre los dos circuitos llegando a pelear el número uno en WPT y quedando solo por detrás de dos parejas de época como Tapia-Coello y Galán-Lebrón. Pero de ilusión no se vive. Ni se gana. Y lo que el 2024 enseñó a Franco fue que el deporte se rige por los resultados, ese juez imparcial que no entiende de emociones ni sentimientos, y que obligaría a decir adiós a la segunda etapa de la pareja argentina. Su siguiente paso sería apostar por un joven talento para cerrar el año. Mike Yanguas sería el elegido y tras un periodo de adaptación en el que tardarían en llegar los resultados, lograrían acabar empastando en el tramo final de 2024 logrando la victoria en Newgiza y dos finales más en Kuwait y Acapulco que hacían presagiar un futuro prometedor. Pero no sería así. El 2025 apuntaba a la continuidad de un proyecto en clara progresión, pero en el deporte hay llamadas que hay que coger. Y al otro lado del teléfono estaba Juan Lebrón que buscaba en el argentino un nuevo status para asaltar la cima. Stupa no dudaría en darle el “sí” para recuperar el paso perdido de la zona más alta del ranking y ya en el primer torneo del año solo les separaría del título la tiranía de los Golden Boys. El río revuelto del boicot de los jugadores al circuito acabaría premiando a unos Stupa y Lebrón que irían como cabeza de cartel al tercer torneo del año en Cancún haciéndose con la victoria. Un título que, a pesar de jugar por momentos a un gran nivel, quedaría en un brindis al sol por los excesos, la presión y la falta de resultados y que acabaría por finiquitar el proyecto a falta de dos torneos para el cierre de año. Así volvería a buscar cobijo de forma temporal en la era 3.0 de Stupa y Di Nenno, pero esta vez lejos de las opciones de victoria. Y así nos plantamos en 2026, el año más duro de la carrera del ‘Rayo’. Una temporada que arrancó de nuevo con Mike Yanguas y en la que a pesar de ganar el FIP Platinum de Albania no lograría encontrar el equilibrio llevándole a encarar el parón veraniego para bsucar nuevos aires, esta vez en un perfil diferente como Jon Sanz. Un acierto que daría resultados rápidos y que ha recuperado para la causa a un jugador que vuelve a lucir regular, completo y ganador que refleja las cuatro finales casi consecutivas logradas, el título del FIP Gold de Belgrado y la eliminación de Chingalán en Rotterdam y Düsseldorf. Un recorrido, largo, intenso y exitoso para un jugador que ya ha cumplido los 30 y que detalla cuál es la envergadura de Stupa en la era moderna del pádel. El mismo bagaje en el que ha logrado títulos todos y cada uno de los años desde su salto a la élite diez temporadas atrás (2017-2026). Tres más como ganador si consideramos los campeonatos Challenger de su primerísima etapa y los FIP de esta última. Como hicieran, entre otros, Bela (1996-2022), Juan Martín (1994-2015), Lima (2009-2022), Sanyo (2011-2022) o Paquito (2014-2023). Casi diez años situado en el top-4 de parejas habiendo rendido con cada compañero con el que ha jugado y que junto a su palmarés son la constatación de que Stupa es ya uno de los jugadores más regulares de la historia del pádel moderno. Y, sí, los integrantes del ‘Club de los Diez’ fueron en algún momento números uno y probablemente Stupa no lo consiga. Pero quizá no le haga falta para tener el estatus que se ha ganado.

articles.title: INDYCAR Driver Jack Harvey Shares Cancer Diagnosis: 'Life Has Delivered A New Fight'
articles.summary: INDYCAR driver and FOX Sports broadcaster Jack Harvey announced he has cancer.
articles.body: INDYCAR driver and FOX Sports broadcaster Jack Harvey announced Tuesday that he has cancer and did not share specifics about his diagnosis. The 33-year-old racer — who drove for Dreyer & Reinbold Racing in the Indianapolis 500 this year while working the rest of the season as a pit reporter on INDYCAR races and as an analyst in the booth on Indy NXT races — said his goals for 2027 have not changed. "My entire career has been about fighting for what’s next," he posted on social media. "The next opportunity. The next chance to prove myself. The next time I could get back in the car and show what I’m capable of. "There have been moments when the path forward was obvious, and plenty when it wasn’t. I’ve had to earn opportunities, fight to keep them, and learn how to keep moving when things didn’t go the way I planned. But through all of it, I’ve never stopped believing that there was something worth fighting for. "Life has delivered a new fight to my doorstep." Harvey has 17 career top-10 finishes in 95 INDYCAR starts since 2017, when he made his debut in the Indianapolis 500. Having raced for Meyer Shank Racing, Schmidt Peterson Motorsports, Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing and Dale Coyne Racing, Harvey started a new challenge in 2025 when he joined FOX Sports as a reporter on telecasts. "My goals for 2027 have not changed," he wrote. "I plan to be on the grid in St. Pete and strapping back into a race car this May in preparation for the Indianapolis 500." Dreyer & Reinbold Racing released a statement of support on Tuesday as well, writing: "Our entire team stands united in support of Jack as he begins his battle with cancer. More than a teammate, Jack is a valued member of our family, and our thoughts and unwavering support are with him and his loved ones as he faces this new challenge. We respectfully ask that Jack's privacy be honored as he focuses on his health and recovery."

articles.title: Indiana HC Curt Cignetti Talks There Being 'No One Like' OSU's Jeremiah Smith
articles.summary: Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti had bold praise for Ohio State Buckeyes superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith.
articles.body: Ohio State Buckeyes superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith continues to draw strong praise from the opposition, a list of people that now includes the head coach of the team that has won 22 consecutive games. "He's taken it up a notch, without question. I think he has nine touchdown catches in the last three Power Four conference games. There's no one like him right now playing at this level," Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti said about Smith at a press conference Monday. "He's a freak, and we're going to have to do a great job on him." No. 5 Indiana (6-0) hosts No. 4 Ohio State (5-1) on Saturday (12 p.m. ET on FOX), with FOX's "Big Noon Kickoff" on site in Bloomington for the Big Ten showdown. Last year, Indiana defeated Ohio State in the Big Ten Championship en route to winning its first national championship in program history. The Hoosiers are coming off a Week 6 scare on the road against the Nebraska Cornhuskers, as they rallied from down 11 points in the fourth quarter to escape with a 20-17 victory. As for the scare in store for Indiana in Week 7, Smith, who already stood out in momentous fashion across his freshman and sophomore seasons, has taken his game to another level this season for Ohio State. In fact, Smith has become the Buckeyes' all-time leader in receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). Prior to Ohio State's Week 6 win against the Maryland Terrapins, he combined for 23 receptions for 423 yards and six touchdowns in wins over the Iowa Hawkeyes and Illinois Fighting Illini. In all, Smith has logged 48 receptions for 916 yards (19.1 yards per reception) and 11 touchdowns, which all lead the Big Ten and are each second in the nation, across Ohio State's six games this season. In 2025, he led the Big Ten with both 87 receptions and 1,243 receiving yards, while leading the conference with 1,315 receiving yards and 15 touchdowns in 2024. FOX Sports' Joel Klatt recently said that Smith is "entering the chat" for the greatest Buckeyes player ever. Meanwhile, Indiana's offense is second in the Big Ten in total yards (462.7 per game) and third in points (40.2 per game) and will face an Ohio State defense that's second in the conference in both opponent total yards (246.8 per game) and opponent points (13.2 per game).

articles.title: 70 países corriendo sin parar: la locura del Mundial Backyard Ultra
articles.standfirst: España, que en 2027 se convertirá junto a Estados Unidos en el país con más pruebas de ultra de circuito cerrado, aspira a colarse en el top 5 este fin de semana en Cartagena
articles.summary: España, que en 2027 se convertirá junto a Estados Unidos en el país con más pruebas de ultra de circuito cerrado, aspira a colarse en el top 5 este fin de semana en Cartagena
articles.body: La resistencia física y mental llevada al límite. La Backyard Ultra vuelve a poner a prueba a los corredores de todo el mundo este sábado 17 de octubre con el Mundial por selecciones, una competición que se disputa de manera simultánea en más de 70 países y en la que España aspira a situarse entre las cinco mejores selecciones. Cartagena será el escenario de la participación española, con un recorrido diseñado para favorecer la acumulación de vueltas y una organización que trabaja contrarreloj ante la previsión de lluvias. Eric Priego, uno de los corredores destacados de la modalidad en España e integrante del combinado nacional, y Luis Ortiz, director técnico del Campeonato de España Individual y del Mundial por Equipos, explicaron en INGRAVIDOS, el programa de trail running, montaña, aventura y outdoor de Radio MARCA, los detalles de una cita que trasciende lo estrictamente deportivo. El objetivo del equipo español está definido. "He visto que alguno lo colgaba en redes y me uno a ellos: hemos coincidido en hacer, al menos como selección, un top 5", explicó Priego durante la entrevista. España ya demostró su competitividad en anteriores ediciones, aunque el recuerdo de los problemas organizativos que afectaron a su clasificación sigue presente. El corredor señaló que el combinado había llegado a situarse en la octava posición, antes de que una incidencia terminara relegándolo a los puestos 12 o 15. En Europa, recordó, España fue tercera, por detrás de Bélgica y Francia. La competencia, en cualquier caso, será exigente. Según las cifras manejadas por Priego, participarán 74 selecciones, con Bélgica, Estados Unidos, Nueva Zelanda y Francia entre las principales candidatas. La ausencia de algunos nombres destacados por lesión abre un escenario incierto en una disciplina en la que la regularidad, la estrategia y la capacidad para soportar el desgaste pueden resultar determinantes. La organización ha diseñado un trazado de tierra compactada, sin asfalto ni zonas técnicas y con apenas nueve metros de desnivel positivo, a orillas del Mar Menor. El propósito es facilitar el ritmo y permitir que los integrantes de la selección española puedan completar el mayor número de vueltas posible. "Hemos buscado un circuito lo más llano posible para que la selección española pueda dar el máximo número de vueltas", explicó Luis Ortiz. La distancia será idéntica a la de las demás sedes internacionales: 6,706 kilómetros por vuelta. La homologación se realiza mediante el envío del recorrido en formato GPX a la organización internacional de Backyard Ultra, que lidera el excéntrico Lazarus Lake, también creador de la Barkley Marathons. La principal preocupación está ahora en el cielo. Las previsiones meteorológicas anuncian lluvia para el fin de semana y el agua podría complicar un recorrido que, en condiciones normales, resulta especialmente favorable. Ortiz descartó contemplar la suspensión como escenario de partida, aunque reconoció que el equipo organizador estudia alternativas para adaptar las instalaciones si las precipitaciones son intensas. Para ello, se han previsto carpas militares con la colaboración del Regimiento de Artillería Antiaérea número 73 de Cartagena, además de 15 espacios habilitados para los participantes. También se prepara un edificio próximo a la salida que permitiría ofrecer refugio a corredores y asistentes. Su principal inconveniente es una escalera que podría convertirse en un obstáculo añadido después de decenas de horas de esfuerzo. La Backyard Ultra tiene una mecánica tan sencilla de explicar como difícil de ejecutar. Los corredores deben completar una vuelta de 6,706 kilómetros en menos de una hora y regresar a la salida a tiempo para comenzar la siguiente. La competición continúa hasta que solo queda un participante capaz de completar el recorrido dentro del tiempo establecido. En este formato, la velocidad no es necesariamente la clave. La capacidad de administrar el esfuerzo, alimentarse, descansar y mantener la concentración durante horas puede marcar la diferencia entre abandonar y seguir adelante. Priego no quiso comprometerse con una cifra definitiva, aunque sí estableció un primer objetivo. "Yo tengo 60. O sea, que 60 las tengo que superar sí o sí", afirmó. La posibilidad de alcanzar las 100 vueltas dependerá, entre otros factores, de la meteorología y de cómo responda su cuerpo. En el anterior Mundial llegó a completar 60 vueltas pese a sufrir una lesión que, según relató, le condicionó durante 18 vueltas. La preparación nutricional será otra de las claves. Después de reconocer que tradicionalmente había comido lo que encontraba durante las carreras, el corredor afrontará esta cita con el asesoramiento de una nutricionista. Como referencia general, apuntó a una ingesta aproximada de 50 gramos de carbohidratos por hora, adaptada a las necesidades individuales. Más allá del Mundial, la entrevista sirvió para constatar el crecimiento de la Backyard Ultra en España. Ortiz recordó que cuando el club Los Mudos Trail organizó su primera prueba en Cartagena, hace cuatro años, no faltaron quienes consideraron una locura la iniciativa. La respuesta de los corredores ha terminado respaldando el proyecto. "Hace cuatro años había seis o siete Backyard; ahora hay cuarenta y tantas, cada día salen nuevas", señaló el director técnico, que considera que el atractivo de la modalidad no se explica únicamente por el desafío físico y mental. La dimensión social también juega un papel importante. La dinámica permite compartir vueltas y horas de esfuerzo con corredores de niveles muy diferentes, algo que no siempre sucede en las carreras convencionales. Un participante puede coincidir durante buena parte de la jornada con atletas que, en una prueba con salida y meta tradicionales, competirían en grupos muy alejados. Priego, que también ejerce como organizador de la Backyard de la Costa Brava, coincidió en destacar la expansión del formato. España se ha convertido, junto a Estados Unidos y Francia, en uno de los países con mayor actividad, hasta el punto de que la proliferación de pruebas ha aumentado la competencia por las plazas clasificatorias para las grandes citas internacionales. El desafío no termina en el recorrido. La preparación de una competición que puede prolongarse durante varios días obliga a la organización a mantener recursos e instalaciones operativos durante mucho tiempo, aunque el número de participantes sea reducido. Ortiz explicó que los corredores comenzarán a competir el sábado a las 14.00 horas, el horario unificado para todas las sedes mundiales. La previsión de una prueba de larga duración ha llevado incluso a gestionar la cobertura de seguros para los 15 integrantes del grupo hasta el miércoles 21 de octubre, una locura logística. "Si ellos dan 100 horas, nosotros estamos 20 horas antes y 20 horas después para desmontar", resumió el responsable técnico, que ha tenido que reservar parte de sus vacaciones para preparar el evento junto a su equipo. El trabajo, sin embargo, no acaba con la cita internacional. Cartagena prepara también la primera edición de la Backyard Ultra del Mar Menor, prevista para el 13 de febrero de 2027 sobre el mismo circuito. La prueba ha completado ya sus 250 dorsales, una muestra más del interés que despierta una modalidad en plena expansión. Con el recorrido preparado, las alternativas frente a la lluvia en marcha y la selección española decidida a pelear por el top 5, Cartagena se convierte este sábado en uno de los centros neurálgicos de la resistencia mundial. Allí, cada hora será una nueva salida y cada vuelta, una oportunidad para acercarse al límite. En la Backyard Ultra, la meta no está marcada de antemano: llega cuando el cuerpo o la mente dicen basta.

articles.title: Illinois high school football rivalry sells out college football stadium ticket allotment
articles.summary: A high school football matchup between two Illinois rivals has sold out its ticket allotment for a game at Northwestern's Ryan Field.
articles.body:
An Illinois rivalry matchup is stirring up a lot of buzz ahead of a big game at Northwestern's Ryan Field .

Just two weeks after the Wildcats opened play for the first time at their brand-new $862 million facility on Friday, Oct. 2, rivals Evanston (IL) and New Trier (IL) are scheduled to play the first high school game — and just the third football game — at the brand-new stadium .

The early hype has lived up to the game's billing. Tickets sold like hotcakes for the 118th matchup between the Wildkits and the Trevians, with nearly 20,000 tickets being sold as of Monday, Oct. 12.

More tickets were available on Ticketmaster starting at 10 a.m. Tuesday, Oct. 13. Fans then had to wait in a queue for a chance to purchase tickets. USA TODAY Sports waited in the queue for over 30 minutes before being able to buy tickets.

USA TODAY Sports reached out to Ryan Sports Ventures, New Trier and Evanston for comment. None of them got back as of publication time.

Tickets were first made available beginning Saturday, Oct. 10. Student tickets were going for $10, while general admission cost $15 and premium seating was set at $50.

Northwestern sold out its opener against Penn State on Friday, Oct. 2, with an announced crowd of 35,000 fans.

In May, Northwestern, Pat Ryan Jr. and the two schools announced the annual rivalry game between Evanston and New Trier would be the third game played at the brand-new stadium. New Trier High is just over five miles from the stadium; Evanston High School is located just two miles from the new Ryan Field.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Carmelo Hayes' Heel Turn with 946, Sheamus, Penta & Stratton's Money in the Bank Wins
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Carmelo Hayes' shocking addition to 946 at the conclusion of Monday night's episode of Raw was reportedly the brainchild of someone who was already in the group.

According to False Finish , 946 leader Royce Keys was the one who inquired about bringing Hayes into the stable.

The main event of Raw saw 946's Keys, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price face The Bloodline's Solo Sikoa and The Usos in a highly anticipated clash that had been weeks in the making.

In the closing moments of the match, an assailant attacked Sikoa with a crowbar before removing the bandana from his face and revealing his identity.

It was Hayes, who had been absent from WWE programming for several weeks, with his most recent match being a loss to then-United States champion Baron Corbin on the Aug. 14 episode of SmackDown.

Melo's absence was a major talking point among fans who were frustrated over his lack of utilization.

In Hayes, 946 added an elite in-ring worker with a ton of charisma and a history of success as a former NXT champion, North American champion and United States champion.

Also, with Keys, Nima, Price, Hayes and Jaida Parker, 946 now has a five-person unit for a WarGames match against The Bloodline at Survivor Series next month, assuming WWE goes in that direction.

TNA Reportedly Expressed Interest in Sheamus for BFG

Before bringing in former AEW star Max Caster to face Moose at Bound For Glory on Sunday, TNA reportedly discussed making a play for a multi-time WWE world champion.

According to False Finish , Sheamus was the "primary name that TNA was considering" to be Moose's opponent at its biggest pay-per-view of the year.

Fightful Select (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats) reported in July that Sheamus was set to leave WWE upon the expiration of his contract, and Fightful Select (h/t Fightful's Ishaan Sharma ) later followed up by reporting that he officially became a free agent on Oct. 1.

Since then, The Celtic Warrior has primarily been linked to AEW with Fightful Wrestling reporting that some "big veteran names" in AEW were pushing for the company to sign him.

The 48-year-old Sheamus is among the most accomplished Superstars in WWE history as a four-time world champion, three-time United States champion, five-time tag team champion and one-time winner of the Royal Rumble, Money in the Bank and King of the Ring.

Because of that, it comes as little surprise that he is reportedly generating interest from multiple companies.

What isn't clear from False Finish's report is if Sheamus rebuffed TNA's interest, prompting them to go with Caster, or if TNA picked Caster despite mutual interest between the company and Sheamus.

If TNA does manage to land Sheamus, it will represent one of the promotion's biggest signings in recent memory, and give it a bona fide main eventer to lean on.

Reported Details Behind Penta, Stratton's MITB Wins

WWE reportedly made some creative changes regarding the winners of the men's and women's Money in the Bank ladder matches over the weekend.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), Penta "wasn't supposed to be" the Money in the Bank winner as of a month ago.

However, WWE's outlook reportedly changed after his strong performance in a losing effort against world heavyweight champion Roman Reigns on the Sept. 14 episode of Raw in Mexico City.

WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News) also reported a significant contributing factor in booking Tiffany Stratton to win the women's Money in the Bank ladder match was the notion that so many fans thought Roxanne Perez would win.

Ultimately, WWE reportedly decided it wanted to do something "different to be different" in the form of making Tiffany a two-time Miss Money in the Bank.

Regardless of how the decisions were made, there are interesting stories to tell with both Money in the Bank contract holders.

Penta already has history with Reigns, but could just as easily cash in on the more vulnerable titleholder in WWE champion Sami Zayn.

Meanwhile, Stratton has been teaming up with WWE women's champion Chelsea Green, which suggests she is ripe for a double-cross.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream to host Finals Games 3 and 4 in much larger arena after days-long drama
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream may have racked up a ton of steals on the court against opponents in this WNBA postseason, but the franchise just got a major assist ahead of the Finals against the Golden State Valkyries.
articles.body: The Atlanta Dream may have racked up a ton of steals on the court against opponents in this WNBA postseason, but the franchise just got a major assist ahead of the Finals against the Golden State Valkyries. On Tuesday, it was announced the WNBA Finals schedule would be altered for Game 3 and Game 4 to accommodate the Dream using State Farm Arena in downtown Atlanta instead of the team’s home base, Gateway Center Arena in nearby College Park, Georgia. The Gateway Center has the smallest capacity in the league at 3,500 and State Farm Arena, home of the NBA’s Atlanta Hawks, holds around 17,000. Game 3, originally scheduled for October 22, will now be played October 21. Game 4 will remain on October 24, but tipoff is moving up to 1 p.m. ET to accommodate the Hawks’ home opener against the Houston Rockets later that night. The Hawks agreed to move the start time of their game to 8:30 p.m. instead of 8 p.m. ET. The WNBA Finals begin Saturday in San Francisco at Chase Center, the home of the Valkyries, which has the fifth-largest capacity in the league at more than 18,000. The series is a 2-2-1-1-1 format. “This is what the players and the fans deserve,” Dream majority owner Larry Gottesdiener said in a statement. “We are grateful to all of the stakeholders who worked together to resolve the conflicts and make this happen.” Both fan bases for the Dream and the Valkyries are sharing the excitement of getting to the WNBA Finals. But the two teams were dealing with vastly different circumstances on where these games will be played – as fervent Atlanta fans were worried they would have massive trouble getting a coveted ticket close to home. The Dream previously used State Farm Arena for some games this season, including the playoffs. But the way the WNBA Finals schedule had originally been constructed, all three of the games Atlanta could host had conflicts at that venue. “We are thrilled that we will be able to accommodate the Dream as they host Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena,” said Andrew Saltzman, president of business enterprise and chief commercial officer for the Hawks and State Farm Arena. “Playing for a championship is special, and we want the Dream to feel the full support of the city during this amazing run.” The Dream advanced to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013 and the Valkyries are reaching the championship stage in just the team’s second season. It’s got the makings of a blockbuster matchup in Angel Reese vs. Gabby Williams. Either Atlanta or Golden State will be a first-time WNBA Finals champion. But the focus had been on the number of seats available – or, in this case, not available. And just like in 2013, there had been a possibility the Dream wouldn’t be able to play in downtown Atlanta in a large arena used heavily for professional basketball with a championship on the line. “We are grateful for the efforts made by numerous stakeholders, including the Dream, the Valkyries, the Hawks, State Farm Arena, and NBC Sports and USA Sports,” WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert said. “The change of venue dramatically expands the seating capacity and ensures that the Dream will be able to provide an extraordinary atmosphere for the first WNBA Finals game to be played in the Atlanta market since 2013. We are pleased that thousands more fans across the Southeast region will have the opportunity to experience the ultimate WNBA action – the WNBA Finals – in person.” The Dream, which joined the WNBA as an expansion team in 2008, used State Farm Arena – then known as Philips Arena – for home games from 2008-2016. But despite having it as a home base during the 2013 WNBA Finals, the Dream had to move from downtown Atlanta to Duluth – a suburb in Gwinnett County – for Game 3 because of Disney On Ice. It was the only home game the Dream hosted, getting swept by the Minnesota Lynx in that best-of-five series. Gateway Center Arena has been the team’s full-time home arena for the last six years. The team will move back to State Farm Arena full time in 2027. Not all WNBA franchises in cities that also have NBA teams have the same ownership or same arena. That applies here: The Dream franchise has a different ownership group than the Hawks. The Valkyries, meanwhile, share owners with their NBA counterpart, the Golden State Warriors. They share Chase Center in San Francisco. And ahead of time, the Valkyries committed to all home games in this Finals being at their home arena. The team previously had announced a Doja Cat concert – scheduled the same night as Game 2 of the WNBA Finals coming up Monday – would be moved if Golden State got that far. Golden State has the home-court advantage against Atlanta and will host Games 1 and 2 and, if necessary, Game 5 and Game 7. The original schedule conflict involved all three games the Dream could host. Game 3, which originally was scheduled for October 22, is the same night as a Sombr concert at State Farm Arena. Game 6, if necessary, also falls on the same date as a Hawks home game, October 29 against the Cleveland Cavaliers. No plan to deconflict with that Hawks game has yet been announced, should the series reach a Game 6. While it’s common for NBA teams to take precedence if there’s a double booking at the team’s home arena – it notably happened to the Hawks in 2023, when a Janet Jackson concert got postponed for a first-round playoff game against the Boston Celtics – there is previous history where WNBA playoff games have been moved away from a team’s home arena over the course of the WNBA’s 30 seasons. Just last year, the Valkyries – shocking the WNBA world by reaching the playoffs in their inaugural season in 2025 – moved a first-round playoff game more than 40 miles away to SAP Center in San Jose, the home of the NHL’s San Jose Sharks. The game was relocated because the Laver Cup, a tennis event, was booked at Chase Center. The Valkyries were swept in that best-of-three series by the Lynx.

articles.title: What We Know About Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson's Ankle Injury
articles.summary: After an injury-plagued training camp, New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson finds himself sidelined once again.
articles.body: After an injury-plagued training camp, New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson finds himself sidelined once again. Henderson suffered a high-ankle sprain during New England's Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, ESPN reported on Tuesday morning. While he is expected to miss multiple weeks, all indications suggest Henderson avoided surgery and could return sooner rather than later. Henderson previously dealt with a Grade 1 ankle sprain during training camp that cost him multiple weeks. The injury didn’t just keep Henderson out of practice, but it also forced him to miss the season opener against the Seattle Seahawks. It’s unclear if this is the same ankle injury, but Henderson has struggled to stay healthy since entering the league as a second-round pick out of Ohio State. Henderson has also struggled on the field this season, but injuries have undoubtedly played a factor in his regression following an impressive rookie season. Through four games, Henderson has rushed for 163 yards (3.9 yards per carry) and just a single touchdown. With Henderson now sidelined, veteran running back Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to step back into a three-down workhorse role. Meanwhile, rookie Corey Kiner should serve as the primary change-of-pace option moving forward. Kiner is coming off a strong performance against the Raiders. After Henderson left the game, Kiner stepped up to rush for 52 yards on six carries (8.7 yards per carry), headlined by a 32-yard run. With the Patriots sitting at 3-2, the time for the offense to click is now in a competitive AFC East. With Henderson sidelined and wide receiver A.J. Brown still on injured reserve, even more pressure continues to fall on the shoulders of quarterback Drake Maye.

articles.title: ¿Grama del parque La Florida para reparar El Campín? La denuncia de Leandro Castellanos y la respuesta del IDRD
articles.standfirst: Extracción de grama en el parque La Florida: IDRD responde a denuncias por traslado a El Campín
articles.summary: Extracción de grama en el parque La Florida: IDRD responde a denuncias por traslado a El Campín
articles.body: Una nueva controversia envolvió el manejo de los escenarios deportivos en Bogotá. El concejal y exfutbolista Leandro Castellanos (Alianza Verde) hizo pública una denuncia ciudadana según la cual se habría extraído césped del Parque La Florida —un espacio de uso público— para trasladarlo al estadio Nemesio Camacho El Campín, cuya gramilla sufrió severos daños tras la realización de eventos masivos. El cabildante y exarquero profesional difundió un video en sus redes sociales en el que se observan zonas sin césped dentro del Parque La Florida, acompañadas de movimiento de maquinaria pesada y camiones. De acuerdo con el seguimiento planteado por Castellanos, las rutas de los vehículos cargados con los rollos de pasto coincidían con trayectos dirigidos hacia El Campín. “¿La grama extraída de una de las canchas del Parque La Florida terminó en el estadio El Campín? Esa es una pregunta que Bogotá necesita resolver. Lo que está mal es afectar una cancha de un parque distrital en donde hay escuelas de formación, clubes deportivos y comunidad que va a hacer recreación y actividad física”, manifestó el concejal. El deterioro del terreno de juego del máximo escenario de los bogotanos —que obligó incluso a trasladar partidos de la Liga BetPlay a municipios vecinos— reabrió el debate sobre el estado en que quedan los campos tras la logística de grandes eventos culturales y quién debe asumir los costos económicos de su restitución. Ante este panorama, Castellanos solicitó a la empresa Sencia, al Instituto Distrital de Recreación y Deporte (IDRD) y a la interventoría la publicación inmediata de facturas, contratos, permisos y registros de salida y recepción del material vegetal. Frente a los señalamientos, el IDRD emitió una respuesta oficial aclarando los trabajos adelantados en el Parque La Florida, aunque sin mencionar de forma directa al estadio El Campín ni a la empresa Sencia. Según precisó el IDRD, la figura legal utilizada contempla una contraprestación en especie, mediante la cual Equiver S.A.S. se compromete a realizar la nivelación, instalación de sistemas de riego y recuperación con nueva cobertura vegetal de los tres campos intervenidos al finalizar el periodo asignado. Frente a la preocupación de la comunidad deportista por la disponibilidad del espacio, el IDRD confirmó que el parque La Florida dispone de 11 canchas de fútbol. Previo a la autorización del permiso, la entidad verificó que las canchas seleccionadas (6, 8 y 9) no contaban con reservas ni asignaciones vigentes, evitando alterar la programación deportiva habitual. Las ocho canchas restantes seguirán prestando servicio normal bajo el contrato regular de mantenimiento de gramas con apoyo de Aguas de Bogotá. Los trabajos técnicos tienen un costo estimado de $444 millones de pesos, los cuales serán asumidos en su totalidad por Equiver S.A.S. sin requerir desembolsos de fondos públicos por parte de la administración distrital. Durante un periodo de seis meses, la empresa privada también velará por el cuidado integral y la preservación del césped en los terrenos intervenidos.

articles.title: Los 4 señalamientos de Eva Ferrer contra Verónica Alcocer que ya investiga la justicia
articles.standfirst: La Fiscalía y la Procuraduría analizan las acusaciones de Eva Ferrer contra la exprimera dama Verónica Alcocer por presunto uso indebido de bienes y otros delitos
articles.summary: La Fiscalía y la Procuraduría analizan las acusaciones de Eva Ferrer contra la exprimera dama Verónica Alcocer por presunto uso indebido de bienes y otros delitos
articles.body: La controversia en el entorno del gobierno de Gustavo Petro ha alcanzado un nuevo punto crítico tras las explosivas declaraciones de la exconsejera presidencial Eva Ferrer. La exfuncionaria de origen español, quien fue una de las personas más cercanas a la exprimera dama Verónica Alcocer, ha formulado una serie de graves acusaciones que abarca desde presunto uso indebido de recursos públicos hasta supuestas redes de corrupción. Las autoridades judiciales y los organismos de control en Colombia, incluidos la Fiscalía y la Procuraduría, han comenzado a actuar sobre estos señalamientos para determinar su veracidad y posible alcance legal. Entre los puntos más delicados expuestos por Ferrer —y que hoy son materia de análisis por parte de la justicia— se destacan: Las declaraciones han generado una inmediata reacción en distintos frentes de la administración pública y el aparato judicial: Hasta el momento, las afirmaciones de Eva Ferrer corresponden a testimonios de prensa que demandan un riguroso proceso de verificación. La Fiscalía General de la Nación y los organismos disciplinarios deberán determinar si existen elementos materiales probatorios —como registros de vuelo, movimientos bancarios, manifiestos de aduana o comunicaciones interceptadas— que sustenten penalmente las acusaciones. El caso continúa en desarrollo mientras los entes de control recopilan los testimonios formales de las partes involucradas.

articles.body:
The Chicago Blackhawks released photos of star center Connor Bedard in his new captain's jersey ahead on Tuesday.

Bedard underwent left shoulder surgery last summer after suffering an injury during offseason training in Vancouver on July 2 . He missed his team's first six games, but Chicago announced its activation of Bedard from the injured non-roster list.

Per the Canadian Press , Bedard is expected to make his season debut on Tuesday evening at home versus the Pittsburgh Penguins.

The 21-year-old Bedard was one of the most lauded prospects in recent memory a few years ago before Chicago selected him with the first overall pick in the 2023 NHL draft. He won the Calder Memorial Trophy as the NHL's Rookie of the Year in 2023-24.

Over his first three seasons (219 games), Bedard has amassed 75 goals and 128 assists. He posted career-high marks in goals (30), assists (45) and points (75) last season.

Chicago has struggled mightily since the 2019-20 season, the last time the Blackhawks made the playoffs. They've finished last in the Central Division each of the last four seasons, although their point total has steadily risen from their 82- or 84-game low or 52 points in 2023-24. Chicago improved to 61 points in 2024-25 and 72 in 2025-26 thanks in part to Bedard's efforts.

This year has gotten off a rough start, especially without Bedard. Thankfully, he's back in the mix and now has the C on his jersey as Chicago looks to turn this season around in short order.

articles.title: Bob Chesney, UCLA Bruins Top List In AP Big Ten Midseason Awards
articles.summary: Bob Chesney and his UCLA Bruins, Jeremiah Smith and Oregon head the list of AP Big Ten midseason awards after Week 6 of the football season.
articles.body: By the looks of it, Bob Chesney is well on his way to fixing the fixer-upper he acquired when UCLA hired him. The No. 12 Bruins have their highest ranking in four years, reached midseason as one of nine unbeaten Football Bowl Subdivision teams and are tied with No. 4 Ohio State and No. 5 Indiana at 3-0 in Big Ten play. Not bad for a team that was picked to finish 13th in the 18-team Big Ten and was 8-16 overall and 6-12 in conference games the previous two years under Deshaun Foster and Tim Skipper. For their accomplishments so far, Chesney was named the Big Ten's top coach and UCLA the most surprising team at the midway point of the season by a vote of Associated Press writers who cover the conference. Chesney, who led James Madison to a 21-6 record over two years and a spot in last season's College Football Playoff, inherited a mess when he was hired last December. There was the predictable roster churn that comes with a new coaching hire, but Chesney got a big win when starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava, now injured, decided to stay. A Big Ten-high 46 transfers, including 11 from James Madison, and 17 freshmen joined the Bruins. A major infusion of donor cash for name, image and likeness spending has helped, but the athletic department as a whole was a financial wreck. Five days before the Bruins' opener, chancellor Julio Frenk fired athletic director Martin Jarmond, the man who hired Chesney. Chesney is the first football coach in UCLA history to start his debut season 5-0. The Bruins lead the Big Ten with 253 yards rushing per game and Wayne Knight, one of the James Madison transfers, is first in the conference with 109.6 yards per game. Their 54-3 win at Maryland two weeks ago was the program's most lopsided in a Big Ten game and in a conference road game since 1955, and their 17-15 win at Oregon last week was their first road win against the Ducks since 2004. Most Surprising Player: Aidan Chiles, QB Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles. He has excelled for the Wildcats after playing one year at Oregon State and two at Michigan State, where he got benched after eight games last season. Chiles has led Northwestern to a 4-1 start, completing 71.4% of his passes for 234.4 yards per game with nine touchdowns and no interceptions. Top Offensive Player: Jeremiah Smith, WR Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. He was the unanimous choice for this award as he puts together what looks destined to be one of the best individual seasons in program history. Smith's 48 catches, 916 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns are second-most in the country. He has gone over 150 yards in four of six games, including two over 200 yards. Top First-Year Transfer: Josh Hoover, QB Indiana's Josh Hoover is third in a line of one-year quarterback transfers signed by Curt Cignetti. Hoover has 17 touchdown passes and no interceptions for the defending national champion Hoosiers. He threw 33 interceptions in 35 games his previous three seasons at TCU. Top Defensive Player: Tobi Osunsanmi, Edge Indiana edge Tobi Osunanmi, who transferred from Kansas State after missing the second half of last season because of injury. He leads the Big Ten with 9.5 tackles for loss and is tied for first with teammate Stephen Daley and Oregon's Matyo Uiagalelei with five sacks. Top First-Year Freshman: Luke Wafle, Edge Southern California defensive end Luke Wafle. He has lived up to his billing as a five-star recruit and No. 1 prospect in the nation by On3/Rivals. Wafle has 27 tackles, six for loss and two sacks, and is among the Trojans' highest-graded defenders by Pro Football Focus. He's missed just two tackles on 264 snaps. Most Disappointing Team: Oregon Oregon edged Michigan for this dubious distinction. The Ducks brought in a highly regarded class of transfers to go with 14 returning starters, including a quarterback projected to be one of the first players taken in the 2027 NFL draft. Their No. 2 preseason ranking was highest in program history. A loss at Oklahoma State in the second game was a red flag. They beat Southern California on the road with backup Dylan Raiola at quarterback for most of the game, but last week's 17-15 home loss to UCLA dropped the Ducks to 3-2 and out of the Top 25. Hottest Seat: Mike Locksley Maryland's Mike Locksley has managed to survive seven mostly underwhelming seasons, but this year's could be the worst. The Terrapins have two wins, and one was against a second-tier Championship Subdivision opponent. If they don't beat Rutgers at home as a 6.5-point favorite this week, they might not win another game. Biggest Injury: Dante Moore, QB Oregon's Dante Moore was on the receiving end of linebacker Desman Stephens II's illegal hit to the head and chest, knocking him out in the second quarter against USC on Sept. 26. Moore threw for 30 touchdowns while leading the Ducks to the College Football Playoff semifinals last year, and they had pinned their hopes on him as they chased the program's first national championship. Moore missed the UCLA game, and his status hadn't been determined for this week's game against Nebraska. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: PSG’s Luis Enrique Hopes Man City Avoids Sanctions After Financial Rules Verdict
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain coach Luis Enrique has come to Manchester City’s defense, saying he hopes the club won’t be stripped of titles after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.
articles.body: Paris Saint-Germain coach Luis Enrique came to Manchester City's defense on Tuesday, saying he hopes the club won't be stripped of titles after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. Back-to-back Champions League winner PSG plays City at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday. City could face sanctions including a huge fine, points deductions or even expulsion from England's top flight. There have also been calls for it to be stripped of trophies it won during a nine-year period in which it was found to have artificially inflated its revenue by more than $1 billion. "I hope everything works out well for Man City because I think what they have done on the pitch has been incredible over the last few years and they certainly deserved to win all the trophies they have won," Luis Enrique said ahead of the Champions League game. "The trophies you win on the pitch remain on the pitch. They deserved to win that and I hope they can avoid the sanction. "But now we have to wait to see what the authorities decide or the judge is going to say." City is under Abu Dhabi ownership and PSG is Qatari-backed. Both clubs have been sanctioned by European governing body UEFA for breaching Financial Fair Play regulations in the past. City is accused of providing misleading information about its finances from 2009-18. During that time, it won three titles. It has appealed the verdict. City defender Ruben Dias said the players were focusing on the pitch, like they did Sunday in a 3-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield. "I feel like when you build yourself as a player, you build yourself against any kind of noise," he said. "Personally, and I really feel like I speak for the whole group, we’re very calm. We trust the club, we’re very calm and we’re very focused on enjoying football." The Associated Press contributed to this report. articles.title: NCAA softball player alleges person threatened to come to her school and kill her over women's sports activism
articles.summary: Kendall Kotzmacher says she reported a kill threat to her Colorado Christian campus after speaking out against transgender athletes in girls' sports.
articles.body: NCAA softball player Kendall Kotzmacher says she reported a threat to come to her college and kill her amid backlash over her advocacy against transgender athletes competing in girls’ and women’s sports, while online targeting has also spread to her teammates. The 20-year-old Colorado Christian University sophomore, recently named a Courage Wins Champion by XX-XY Athletics, told OutKick that the hostility has intensified as her public profile has grown. "I had a person say that they were gonna come to the school and kill me. That one was a little scary," Kotzmacher said. Kotzmacher said she reported the threat to her school and had documented other concerning messages over the summer. Asked whether anyone had been arrested, she said no. "I’ve been getting a lot of people telling me to go kill myself or that I don’t deserve to be alive or that I should die, a bunch of stuff like that, which has been really difficult to hear," she said. FINAL SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM RALLY OF THE 2026 REGULAR SEASON PITS SUPPORTERS AGAINST TRANS ACTIVISTS IN MINNESOTA Knowing that strangers can identify where she attends college has added to her fear. "I think people knowing where I go to school has been a little bit scary just because I never know if someone’s going to show up or what’s going to go on," she said. The backlash has also left Kotzmacher concerned about the teammates who publicly support her. She said one person replied to teammates’ comments on her social media posts, visited their accounts and looked up their names and statistics. "I think I want to protect them as much as possible," she said. "So trying to make sure that they’re not getting any of the backlash and that it’s kind of just on me has been a focus of mine." Kotzmacher said she offered in the team’s group chat to remove their names from her social media and make clear they were not involved in her advocacy. Her teammates rejected the offer, she said. "And they’re like, absolutely not. Like, we’re in this together. We’re going to be supportive of you," Kotzmacher recalled. "Like, we’re all here for you, which has been so refreshing to hear because I didn’t really get that last year." Kotzmacher, a sophomore catcher and infielder who previously attended Western Michigan University, transferred this past summer after In her September Fox News op-ed, she attributed her transfer from Western Michigan to a lack of coaching support and pressure in coursework. Her advocacy began after White Bear Lake High School lost 3–2 to Champlin Park in the 2025 Minnesota Class AAAA state semifinals. Champlin Park, whose team included a transgender pitcher, subsequently won the championship. articles.title: Steelers Week 5 grades: Offense has most complete performance of the year
articles.summary: Steelers Week 5 grades.
articles.body:
Don't look now, but the Pittsburgh Steelers' offense is getting hot. They scored a season-high 34 points against the Indianapolis Colts, and are averaging just over 30 points over their last three games.

As we do each week, Joey Bray and I will hand out grades for the previous game's performances, so let's get into it.

Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers put up another solid performance against the Colts, finishing the day going 22-of-31 for 235 yards and three touchdowns. This marked his third straight game with three or more touchdown passes, tying a franchise record held by Terry Bradshaw and Ben Roethlisberger. He was decisive, he used the entire field, and he protected the ball – you can't ask for much more than that. Grade: A

Joey Bray: Rodgers started this game with 11 consecutive completions. This game also marked the first time since December of 2021 that Rodgers has thrown for three or more touchdown passes in three consecutive contests. I was most impressed by how Rodgers moved around the pocket. The Colts' pass rush is not very good, but Rodgers deserves some credit for the way he was able to maneuver the pocket in this one. You have to be impressed with the way Rodgers performed in this one. Grade: A

Jarrett Bailey: Do you know who leads all running backs with at least 25 touches in total EPA over the last three weeks? Did you guess Jaylen Warren because the heading says Jaylen Warren and this is a Steelers site? Great job, you're correct. Yes, Warren has been the most efficient running back with the ball in his hands for the last three weeks, and he had another career day against the Colts with 188 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns. He's turning into a superstar in real time. Grade: A+

Joey Bray: The Steelers running back is third in the NFL in scrimmage yards at his position, behind only Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs. This was the third consecutive game of over 100 scrimmage yards for Warren, who has been the Steelers' best player this season. As we head into Week 6, Warren is averaging a whopping 5.9 yards per carry, behind only James Cook and Kenneth Walker. Warren's efficiency this season has simply been out of this world. Grade: A+

Jarrett Bailey: It wasn't the best day for DK Metcalf numbers wise (three catches, 12 yards) but he did have a key block on Jaylen Warren's long touchdown reception. Germie Bernard also stepped in and caught six passes for 80 yards, while Pat Freiermuth added a pair of touchdowns. Overall, a strong day from the other skill players around Warren. Grade: B

Joey Bray: Jaylen Warren was the best player on the field yesterday. Pat Freiermuth had a great game in which he scored a pair of touchdowns, moving him into a tie for the most receiving touchdowns by a tight end this season. Those performances alone carry this grade. The receiver room was lackluster, but was without Michael Pittman Jr., as well as Roman Wilson and Ben Skrownek who left with injuries in the first half. Germie Bernard led all receivers in yards and catches. Despite two early drops, the young receiver looked the part in his first real opportunity in the Steelers offense. With how Warren and Freiermuth played, it's hard to be that upset with the lackluster receiver room. The Bernard performance was also encouraging, which certainly helps their case. Grade: A

Jarrett Bailey : Aaron Rodgers was the least pressured quarterback in the league in Week 5. After being sacked five times against the Browns, that's a complete 180 from the unit. Warren's big day on the ground was also sprung from huge run lanes opened up. Easily the best day the offensive line has had all year, and the best Steelers' offensive line single week in recent memory. Grade: A+

Joey Bray: This young Steelers offensive line is bound to have some growing pains, as we saw against Cleveland. However, performances like the one they had yesterday against Indianapolis make you confident in the future of their group. Rodgers was only sacked once, and the offensive line gave Rodgers enough time to slowly maneuver through the pocket even when there was pressure. We already discussed just how efficient Warren was with his 6.7 yards per carry in the contest. It was an overall clean game from an offensive line that is starting to trend up. Grade: A+

Jarrett Bailey: The secondary still has a good bit to clean up. Jaquan Brisker got beat a couple times, and there still appears to be too many miscommunications that lead to chunk plays. That said, Asante Samuel Jr. had a pair of really nice pass breakups to prevent touchdowns, and it was a much better performance than the one we saw in Week 5. Grade: C+

Joey Bray: You know what? The secondary ended up doing better than I thought given how limited they were this week, although I'm not certain how much credit to give them considering Colts Daniel Jones was incredibly inaccurate throwing the ball down the field. Asante Samuel Jr. posted one of the better games of his Steelers career with four passes defended. This group certainly could use a boost, but looked the part against what was an overall mediocre Colts passing attack. Grade: C

Jarrett Bailey: The biggest surprise of the week for me was how good the Steeler's run defense was without Derrick Harmon. Credit to Yahya Black, Sebastian Joseph-Day, and Gabriel Rubio for stepping up in their increased roles on Sunday, as well as Cam Heyward and Keeanu Benton, of course. Jonathan Taylor totaled just 45 yards – that's a good day at the office. Grade: A

Joey Bray: No Derrick Harmon? No problem. The Steelers seem to have Jonathan Taylor's number. The star running back amassed just 45 yards on the ground with his 15 carries. The Colts only rushed for 66 yards as a team. After giving up several rushes of over 20 yards last week against Cleveland, this was a resounding response from the run defense. Grade: A+

Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more!

articles.title: Alistair Overeem tells Rico Verhoeven to ‘stop hiding’, box him at Fury vs. Joshua card
articles.summary: Fury vs. Joshua will take place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff
articles.body:
Alistair Overeem wants to be part of the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua boxing card on Dec. 11, and he wants Rico Verhoeven standing across the squared circle.

Overeem shared a post on social media suggesting the bout after mentioning his interest in transitioning to boxing, and issued a callout on his Instagram stories.

"Stop hiding," Overeem wrote. "Let's make history."

Fury vs. Joshua takes place at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, and airs live on Netfilx.

Verhoeven was part of a massive boxing show this past May in Egypt, where he lost via controversial 11th-round stoppage in his boxing debut against heavyweight champion Oleksandr Usyk.

Prior to that match, Verhoeven remained undefeated in kickboxing for over a decade, reigning as the GLORY heavyweight champion. He was slated to face Overeem in 2021, but the MMA veteran withdrew due to an injury.

Overeem competed in kickboxing a year later, but his decision victory over Badr Hari was later overturned for a doping violation .

The former Strikeforce titleholder won four of his past six UFC bouts, all by knockout, between 2018 and 2021, including a first-round stoppage over Sergei Pavlovich. His UFC run also includes wins over former and future champions Fabricio Werdum, Frank Mir, Brock Lesnar, Junior dos Santos and Andrei Arlovski.

articles.title: L'Inter sconfitta 3-4 dal Club Brugge
articles.summary: Serata amara per l'Inter, sconfitta a San Siro dal Club Brugge per 3-4 nella seconda giornata della Fase Campionato della Champions League 2026/27. I nerazzu...
articles.body:
Serata amara per l'Inter, sconfitta a San Siro dal Club Brugge per 3-4 nella seconda giornata della Fase Campionato della Champions League 2026/27. I nerazzurri partono bene, aggrediscono la partita, ma restano incastrati nella grande organizzazione del Club Brugge, bravo a lasciar sfogare i nerazzurri per poi colpire una volta che i ritmi iniziali si abbassano. Il vantaggio arriva al 30' con un rigore perfetto di Tresoldi, dopo che Forbs era stato atterrato in area da Calhanoglu al termine di una ripartenza fulminea. L'Inter cresce, colpisce una traversa con Calhanoglu, poi Lautaro trova il gol del pareggio al termine del primo tempo con un movimento da grande attaccante. La ripresa inizia con un'Inter vivace che ha diverse occasioni per raddoppiare, soprattutto con Lautaro e Dimarco, ma il Brugge trova il gol dell'1-2 con Tresoldi, bravo ad approfittare di un'incomprensione tra Akanji e Martinez. I belgi giocano bene e mettono in difficoltà l'Inter: su un tiro di Forbs respinto da Martinez arriva anche la tripletta di Tresoldi, che sembra chiudere la partita. Nel finale però Lautaro segna ancora su una respinta di Sommer su tiro di Sucic, ma il Brugge rimette due gol di vantaggio con Vermant lanciato in contropiede solo contro Martinez. Nel recupero il gol di Bonny serve solo a ritoccare il tabellino: finisce 3-4 per il Brugge, l'Inter cercherà di conquistare i suoi primi punti in Champions League settimana prossima, mercoledì 21 ottobre contro lo Shakhtar, sempre a San Siro

L'Inter inizia con tante novità rispetto alla partita di sabato contro il Parma: tornano dall'inizio Akanji, Bastoni, Barella, Zielinski e Lautaro, con la conferma di Calhanoglu in regia, degli esterni, di Thuram davanti e Bisseck spostato sulla destra in difesa. Il Brugge è squadra insidiosa e organizzata, ma l'Inter inizia al meglio con aggressività e energia. La pressione alta dei nerazzurri induce ripetutamente i belgi all'errore, con tanto campo libero lasciato soprattutto sulla fascia destra dove agisce Diouf. Al 3' una sua galoppata favorisce il primo tiro della partita di Calhanoglu, che da posizione difficile centra Sommer. Bisseck e Akanji giocano d'anticipo sugli attaccanti del Brugge: al 5' Bisseck sovrasta Tresoldi e serve subito Thuram in verticale, il francese entra in area ma il suo tiro incrociato esce di poco largo. Sei minuti più tardi ci prova Lautaro con una conclusione potente dal limite, ma il suo destro non è preciso. Al 17' ancora Lautaro calcia di prima servito da un cross basso di Diouf, insolitamente a sinistra, ma il suo tentativo viene murato e deviato in angolo da un difensore. L'Inter macina gioco e vince tanti duelli, ma quando i ritmi si abbassano il Club Brugge riesce a ragionare: il 4-5-1 iniziale di Leko è in realtà un dinamico 4-2-3-1, con tanti inserimenti offensivi dei centrocampisti, in particolare del mobilissimo Vetlesen e l'esperto Vanaken, che di fatto gioca alle spalle di Tresoldi. Al minito 21 arriva la prima sortita offensiva dei belgi con uno spunto di Forbs che parte da destra ed entra in area: contrastato, il pallone arriva a Vanaken che calcia centrando in pieno Bisseck, che salva la porta nerazzurra. Il Brugge cresce e conquista territorio alzando il suo baricentro: al 26' sugli sviluppi di un corner Tresoldi si esibisce in una girata potente, con il pallone che si stampa sull'incrocio dei pali. La partita è più accesa che mai: al 28' l'Inter manovra splendidamente con una delle sue giocate codificate. Thuram fa da sponda per Lautaro che va subito in verticale dove Zielinski scatta verso la porta a prendersi tutto il campo lasciato libero dalla difesa dei belgi. Il polacco arriva in area ma al momento del tiro viene rimontato dal rientro improvviso di Vetlesen che mura la sua conclusione. Sull'angolo i nerazzurri si fanno trovare impreparati: Forbs anticipa Zielinski prima che possa provare il tiro al volo e si trova con la strada libera fino all'area dell'Inter, dove viene steso dalla scivolata di Calhanoglu. Dal dischetto si presenta Tresoldi che calcia alla perfezione spiazzando Martinez: 0-1 per il Club Brugge al 30'. Tre minuti più tardi l'Inter reagisce con rabbia e determinazione: Lautaro controlla in area, scarica per Calhanoglu che dopo una finta calcia fortissimo, colpendo in pieno la traversa. Sulla respinta Barella è troppo scoordinato per colpire e il pallone finisce altissimo. Il Brugge però continua a trovare spazio in ripartenza: Virgili viene lanciato sulla sinistra. Lo spagnolo sfida Bisseck nell'uno contro uno e calcia a giro, senza trovare la porta. La squadra di Chivu però cresce ed è disposta a correre qualche rischio per cercare il pareggio: al 36' Lautaro trova la rete con un colpo di testa, ma il Toro è partito in fuorigioco sulla punizione perfetta di Calhanoglu. Il Brugge continua a provarci, ma al 40' Vanaken dopo aver recuperato palla a metà campo invece di servire Virgili liberissimo decide di andare da Forbs dalla parte opposta. L'attaccante tira, ma il suo tentativo è deviato in angolo. Verso il finale di tempo l'Inter alza decisamente i giri del motore: al 42' Lautaro si scalda con un doppio tentativo murato due volte da Spileers, poi due minuti più tardi trova il gol del pareggio. L'Inter riparte in maniera fulminea fin dalla sua area di rigore: Martinez recupera palla in presa bassa, serve Zielinski che con un passaggio in verticale va direttamente da Thuram. Il francese arriva in area, trova Dimarco che di tacco prolunga per Lautaro, che da grande attaccante usa il corpo per sbilanciare il difensore, si gira e colpisce: 1-1, Inter che rimette la partita in equilibrio subito prima dell'intervallo.La ripresa inizia con la marea nerazzurra che sembra poter esondare, con tutti i giocatori coinvolti in fase offensiva: prima ci prova Bastoni con un tiro impreciso, poi al 50' tocca a Thuram che con il destro dal limite non inquadra la porta. Al 56' Lautaro ha un'occasione clamorosa: sfruttando un rimpallo favorevole l'argentino si trova solo in area, mette a sedere Sommer con una finta ma sbaglia il tiro, che viene deviato con la punta del piede dal portiere svizzero. Quattro minuti più tardi il gol viene sfiorato da Dimarco, che colpisce al volo su un cross da destra di Barella, mandando alto di pochissimo. Il Club Brugge però è squadra organizzata e astuta: su un lancio lungo Forbs si infila alle spalle di Dimarco causando un'incomprensione tra Akanji e Martinez, uscito dalla sua area. Il pallone passa e Tresoldi deve solo depositare nella porta sguarnita: i belgi tornano in vantaggio, 1-2. Chivu cerca forze fresche inserendo Esposito per Thuram e Sucic per Calhanoglu, ma l'Inter nella fase centrale della ripresa subisce le iniziative del Brugge che colpisce un palo con Virgili al 70' prima che Potts impegni Martinez in una grande parata. Al 74' Esposito controlla in area, si gira e tira, ma il suo tentativo è bloccato da Sommer. Sul ribaltamento di fronte arriva il terzo gol del Brugge, ancora con Tresoldi: Forbs solo in area calcia, Martinez riesce a respingere in qualche modo ma non può nulla sul tentativo dell'attaccante che a porta vuota completa la sua tripletta. Quando sembra che l'Inter non abbia più la forza per reagire Lautaro riapre la partita: Bonny, entrato per barella, trova Sucic al limite. Il croato calcia forte ma centrale, la respinta di Sommer però arriva dritta sui piedi di Lautaro che sigla la rete del 2-3. Il finale è incandescente: Diouf ci prova da fuori, ma Sommer blocca, così come sul taglio di Lautaro su cross basso da sinistra. All'87' Vermant allarga il vantaggio: l'attaccante scappa in profondità e supera Martinez in uscita con uno scavetto preciso. Nel lungo recupero c'è ancora tempo per l'Inter per rientrare nuovamente in partita, con Bonny che segna il suo primo gol in Champions League al termine di una bella azione personale. Alla fine però è ancora Vermant a impegnare Martinez con un tiro dal limite deviato in angolo: è l'ultima emozione di un match infinito, che termina 3-4 per il Club Brugge. L'Inter cercherà i suoi primi punti nella Champions League 2026/27 settimana prossima, mercoledì 21 ottobre, sempre a San Siro contro lo Shakhtar Donetsk.

The entire TV schedule for the Wildcats' 2026-27 season was announced Tuesday, and it won't require staying up extra late too often. Other than the Maui Invitational, Arizona has only four games scheduled to start at 8 p.m. or later Tucson time.

As for who is airing the games, that's where it gets more complicated. Including the three exhibition games, Arizona has 15 on linear ESPN networks (ESPN, ESPN2 and ESPNU), six on linear Fox networks (FOX/FS1), four on linear CBS channels (CBS/CBS Sports Network), two on truTV and one on TNT.
