articles.title: How Washington football can reshape itself in back half of 2026
articles.summary: Jedd Fisch is exploring all angles to improve the Washington Huskies in the back half of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The first six games of the 2026 season weren't kind to Jedd Fisch and the Washington Huskies , as they sit at 3-3 on the year and 0-3 in Big Ten play following three consecutive losses to Minnesota, USC, and Iowa after a nonconference slate where the team looked shaky, to say the least.

As Fisch looks ahead to the back half of the season, he stated after his team's 41-24 loss to the Hawkeyes on Friday that he wanted to reset where the Huskies are at the halfway point, and expanded on what that should look like.

"We're sitting there; we have two games that we lost by three and four points, and I felt like against SC we were in a place to win the game, and we didn't get it done. Against Minnesota, we started off awfully slow and then played pretty well in the second half, played really well on defense, and had some chances there offensively," Fisch said on Monday.

As Washington's coaching staff tries to figure things out quickly after three straight losses, following an offseason of setting fairly high expectations for the program coming off a 9-4 2025 campaign, Fisch emphasized taking a long look at everything around his program, which has appeared to be in disarray all year.

"What do we need to do? What is the reality of the situation? What do we want to do to make sure that we're getting better? And as we look at each player, how do we get them better?" he added about the messaging to his players. "And as we talk to each player, and the messaging of the team, it was a matter of nobody would've predicted the situation we were in running the football...so where we have to reset is what type of offense do we need to run the next six weeks to put ourselves in a position to score more points?"

"Defensively, how do we get ourselves in a spot where each week we're continuing to get better and not letting a game like that affect the next game? But in terms of messaging, our guys understand we are in this thing together."

Following Friday's loss, the Huskies are sitting at No. 12 in the Big Ten in scoring defense, allowing 22.2 points per game, while the offense ranks No. 16, posting just 26.2 points per game, after finishing No. 4 in scoring offense and No. 5 in scoring defense in 2025.

articles.title: Olise sees red as Viking FK hold Bayern in dramatic six-goal stalemate
articles.summary: On a balmy evening in south-west Norway, Bayern Munich were held to a shock draw with Viking FK. Vincent Kompany's battled back to lead despite a two-goal de...
articles.body:
On a balmy evening in south-west Norway, Bayern Munich were held to a shock draw with Viking FK. Vincent Kompany's battled back to lead despite a two-goal deficit, but Michael Olise's red card enabled the host's to strike late for an historic 3-3 stalemate.

Similar to their woes in the opening seconds against Augsburg last Saturday, Bayern shipped another goal inside just two minutes this evening. Viking FK skipper Zlatko Tripic's corner nodded in by Gianni Stensness, climbing above Kim Min-Jae and Jonathan Tah in the box.

Going slightly more according to the script, Arild Östbö was a busy man between the posts thereafter. The 35-year-old produced a number of strong saves to keep out Konrad Laimer, Michael Olise, Luis Díaz and Harry Kane. Bayern looked to be gaining momentum and fast.

However, their front-footed approach soon went against them six minutes before the break. With all ten outfield players pushed into their host's half, Erik Botheim threaded a neat pass into Peter Christiansen who held off Nathaniel Brown to finish into the bottom right corner.

Making a trio of changes at the interval, Vincent Kompany called upon Upamecano, Davies and Saibari in a bid to turn things around. They did just that when Kristoffer Haugen fouled Laimer, presenting Kane with a penalty which halved the deficit in Stavanger.

Some last-ditch blocks kept the Norwegian side in front past, but Bayern's pressure was unrelenting. As the clock struck an hour, a routine Joshua Kimmich delivery was headed in by Kane lurking at the back post. Now, the travelling Bavarian voices could be heard.

Further drama ensued when Kane and Laimer combined to find Luis Díaz, converting from close range and a crucial lead. That preceded a red card for Michael Olise, picking up a pair of yellow cards for a professional foul followed by lightly tossing the ball into Tripic's face.

With the numerical advantage in their favour for the remaining quarter of an hour, Viking embodied their namesake, marauding forward in waves. They would get their just rewards when Tripic's cross glanced off the head of Herman Haugen which secured a famous draw.

articles.title: Kvapil Chases Victory As CARS Tour Finale Hits South Boston
articles.summary: The CARS Tour wraps up its 2026 campaign this Saturday at South Boston Speedway, and the stakes couldn’t get any higher. Caden Kvapil has already locked up t...
articles.body:
The CARS Tour wraps up its 2026 campaign this Saturday at South Boston Speedway, and the stakes couldn't get any higher. Caden Kvapil has already locked up the Late Model Stock championship, but he isn't resting on his laurels. He wants to end the year exactly how he started it: with a checkered flag in his hand. The track hosts the finale for the fifth time, marking the first season-ending race here since 2021.

Mason Walters faces a tougher challenge in the Pro Late Model division. He holds a points advantage but needs a flawless performance to clinch the title. One mistake could hand the championship to Conner Jones, who trails but still has a mathematical shot. The field is stacked with local talent, making every lap a battle for survival in the tight .400-mile oval.

Caden Kvapil enters the weekend with massive momentum after securing the LMSC title at Newport Speedway. His team has dominated the season, winning six Late Model Stock races total. Four of those victories came on the CARS Tour, while two were Triple Crown wins. That consistency makes him the clear favorite, yet he refuses to take the final race for granted.

He knows that winning at South Boston would be the perfect bookend to a stellar year. "I'm definitely feeling really excited to go to South Boston and not have to worry about points," Kvapil said, according to Short Track Scene . The pressure is off for the title, but the pride remains. He aims to put the No. 04 JR Motorsports car in Victory Lane one more time.

"Every race you go to, you want to win. If I could start and end the CARS Tour season with a win, that'd be really awesome for me," Kvapil added. "I'm hoping to get [JR Motorsports] into Victory Lane one more time." This mindset separates good drivers from great ones. He isn't just racing for a trophy; he's racing for legacy.

Mason Walters controls his own destiny in the PLM Tour standings, but the margin for error is razor-thin. Setzer Racing & Development has fielded a competitive car all year, and Walters has driven it with precision. He admits he didn't see a championship coming when the season began. "I really didn't expect [a PLM Tour championship] going into this year," Walters said.

Now he has a chance to cement his reputation as a top short track prospect. A maximum points night at Newport two weekends ago put him in this position. One more consistent, trouble-free race on Saturday will seal the deal. "I feel confident about everybody on my team," Walters said. That confidence is well-earned after a season of hard work.

Conner Jones isn't giving up without a fight. He would have preferred a smaller points deficit, but he knows the math still works. The race is only 100 laps, which is plenty of time for chaos to unfold. "It's definitely going to be tough to win," Jones said. He needs Walters to falter and then capitalize on every opportunity.

South Boston Speedway is a brutal testing ground for any driver. The .400-mile track features 125 laps for the LMSC cars and 100 for the PLM machines. History shows that past winners like Josh Berry and Bobby McCarty know how to handle the pressure. The local weekly field is one of the most competitive in the southeast, adding extra grit to the entry list.

With 27 cars entered in the LMSC race, the pack will be tight. Drivers like Ronnie Bassett Jr. and Chase Burrow will be hunting for wins too. The PLM field is smaller but no less dangerous. This isn't just a race; it's a collision of championship hopes and pride. The first car to cross the line takes the glory, while the others settle for second place.

Broadcast coverage starts at 8:30 p.m. ET on Saturday via FloRacing. Fans will see the conclusion of a season filled with drama and speed. The CARS Tour has delivered a thrilling year, and South Boston is the perfect place to close the book. Expect contact, expect battles, and expect a new champion crowned in Virginia.

The action moves west immediately after the South Boston finale. On Saturday, Oct. 17, the October Classic takes place at Kevin Harvick's Kern Raceway, where the SPEARS CARS Tour Southwest is heading. That event will decide the 2026 Pro Late Model championship for the Southwest region. Robby Sawyer leads the standings, but the 125-lap feature promises a similar fight for the title.

articles.title: Locomotive FC eye No. 1 seed after securing home-field advantage
articles.summary: EL PASO, Texas (KTSM) — El Paso Locomotive FC secured home-field advantage for the first round of the USL Championship playoffs with a 2-1 victory over Orang...
articles.body:
EL PASO, Texas ( KTSM ) — El Paso Locomotive FC secured home-field advantage for the first round of the USL Championship playoffs with a 2-1 victory over Orange County SC on Saturday. However, the team is approaching its last two matches of the season with a "prove it" mentality, as their main goal is to secure the No. 1 seed in the Western Conference.

"We have that mentality of we haven't done anything, and I think that's what's keeping us performing," said Locomotive FC defender, Ricky Ruiz. "Knowing that we have a goal to reach and nothing's accomplished yet. We were in this position last year where we clinched a home playoff spot, and we all know how that worked out. So nothing's nothing's accomplished yet. I think everybody [on the team] knows the situation we're in, so no one's satisfied and we're we're still hungry for more."

After briefly stumbling to begin October play with a 3-1 loss to Lexington SC that ended a historic nine-game unbeaten streak, Saturday's win kept the Locos on track to push for the top spot in the West.

"[It was] very important to stop the bleeding. You take a bad result and then you get back on it and say, 'okay, this is who we are. This is our mentality,'" said Locomotive FC Head Coach Junior Gonzalez.

Currently, El Paso sits atop the West with 50 points with only two matches left in the regular season, but securing all six points and the No. 1 seed won't be easy. Their last two opponents will be Sacramento Republic FC — third in the West — whom the Locos are only five points ahead of in the standings, and rival New Mexico United — second in the West — whom they lead by only a point.

However Gonzalez said these opponents are the perfect tests ahead of the playoffs.

"We're up for the challenge. We're excited. I was telling the guys today on video we want to play top teams. We want to show that we can beat those top teams here at the tail end of the season to prepare us for what's to come in the postseason," Gonzalez said.

Saturday's match against Sacramento kicks off at 7 p.m. at Southwest University Park. You can also stream the match on ESPN+.

articles.title: The Sun Belt conference is realigning. Here's why
articles.summary: The face of college athletics is changing again.
articles.body:
The Sun Belt Conference announced Monday that it would be realigning. This came shortly after James Madison University Dukes (JMU) decided to pack its bags and head to the American conference. The move is set to take place in 2028.

In a time when NIL and TV rights deals have become the face of college football, schools want what's best for their programs and the athletes. Conferences rake in hundreds of millions of dollars, and the schools associated with those conferences want a piece of the pie. When the bakery runs out of goods, you go to a better one with more options.

According to Sports Illustrated , administrators at JMU and Appalachian State have privately told boosters that the league is undercompensated under the current TV agreement. With the departure of JMU, the Sun Belt will drop to 13 teams.

Sun Belt commissioner Keith Gill said, "Since expanding to 14 football-playing members, the Sun Belt Conference has experienced the best four-year stretch in the conference's 50-year history."

"With James Madison's recent announcement of its planned departure, the conference leadership will examine and evaluate all opportunities as it continues its work to ensure the sustained rise of the Sun Belt Conference—the premier FBS non-autonomy conference in the country."

The Conference has assured that it will remain competitive across multiple sports, promote rivalries, and pursue excellence at a reasonable cost.

Board of Directors President Dr. Kyle Marrero said, "Through a tumultuous period in collegiate athletics, the Sun Belt has remained steadfast in its commitment to regional rivalries, geographic alignment and broad-based competitive excellence-pillars that have ushered in the most successful era in the conference's history."

JMU might be the first to realize how much money is on the line in these new TV deals, and soon everyone else will follow suit.

articles.title: Yankees Must Target Ozzie Albies Over Sean Murphy After Playoff Sweep
articles.summary: The Yankees got swept by the Rays. They need a star now. Ozzie Albies offers a better path than Sean Murphy for a title run.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees season ended on Wednesday, October 7, after the Tampa Bay Rays won the series 3-0. The team needs a star infielder to replace Jazz Chisholm Jr. if he leaves in free agency. The best move is to trade for Atlanta Braves star Ozzie Albies. A deal for catcher Sean Murphy is a waste of time and money. Albies has the track record to anchor the infield for the next decade.

Jazz Chisholm Jr. is a pending unrestricted free agent and his 2026 season was shaky. The Yankees face a major decision on whether to bring him back. If they do not re-sign him, a massive hole opens in the middle of the diamond. Heavy reported that the team must find a replacement if Chisholm walks. Ozzie Albies stands out as the only logical answer. He has been a star throughout his entire career and fits the power needs of the Bronx.

A top trade candidate recently appeared in rumors regarding Albies. Bleacher Report's Joel Reuter suggested the Braves might move on during a larger retooling. According to the source, Albies posted a .299 on-base percentage and a mediocre 88 OPS+ in 1,350 plate appearances during the past two years. This dip in production makes him available now. The Yankees can buy low on a player who has already proven his worth.

Some fans might look at catcher Sean Murphy as a fix. Heavy suggested the Yankees could land him in exchange for prospect Jace Avina. The catch is that New York would have to take on parts of Murphy's six-year, $73 million contract. Eight Major League Baseball years have seen him split time between the Braves and the Athletics. Across 637 games played, he totaled 295 RBIs and 96 home runs. But he has not been great in recent seasons.

Trading for Murphy only solves a backup catcher need while leaving the infield weak. The Yankees do not need to break the proverbial prospect bank for a backup. They need a cornerstone player. Albies offers a clear upgrade over Murphy because he plays a position of greater scarcity and impact. The $73 million price tag for Murphy is a glaring red flag for the front office. The Yankees should not tie up payroll on a declining catcher when a star second baseman is on the table.

The case for Albies is built on his long history of excellence. Joel Reuter observed that the Braves have been Albies' sole team throughout his 10-year career. He accumulated 25.7 WAR while securing four All-Star selections and two Silver Slugger awards. These are not just numbers; they represent years of consistent elite play. Albies once again displayed surface-level power production even alongside the recent slump.

The Braves are looking to retool, which gives the Yankees a unique window to act. If the Braves decide to make Albies available, the Yankees should pursue him right away. He is among the players who the team should have on their radar this offseason. The risk of waiting for free agency is too high. The Rays swept the Yankees in the Division Series, and the team cannot afford another offseason of uncertainty.

articles.title: ‘It’s time for me to pop back out’: Keyshawn Davis claims to have reached deal to face Richardson Hitchins

articles.body:
The living wild card that is Keyshawn Davis has made a public appearance just recently, and in a social media post he claims to have secured a fight against Richardson Hitchins which will take place this December.

"Buddy finally accepted the fight," Keyshawn said. "It's time for me to pop back out…'cause this fight in December, this sh-t personal. And I don't lose personal fights. So I'm going to start popping back out. [Hitchins], I'm on your ass, December, and I'm going to beat your ass. Be there."

Hitchins, who's now aligned with Zuffa, is in desperate need of an opponent with a credible name if he's to advance his career any further than it is now, but we'll have to wait for a more formal announcement to provide any more details.

articles.title: Reaction mixed to school board's vote on Citizens Field, new Buchholz stadium
articles.summary: Last week, the Alachua County School Board voted to rebuild Citizens Field and a new stadium for Buchholz football, resulting in passionate community reactio...
articles.body:
Last Tuesday, the Alachua County School Board decided to drastically change high school football in Gainesville .

The five-member school board voted 3-2 to officially purchase Citizens Field from the City of Gainesville and rebuild the facility built in 1948, along with funding the construction of a new stadium at Buchholz . The estimated cost for Citizens Field comes in at $25 million and $16 million for the new stadium at Buchholz to bring it to $41 million.

The timetable for completion remains uncertain for now, but the vote means an end to the sharing of Citizens Field by Buchholz, Gainesville High and Eastside – an arrangement in place since 1990 when the Bobcats and Hurricanes left Florida Field to move across town.

The Gainesville Sun spoke to Buchholz Athletic Director Thomas Pankey, defensive coordinator and former head coach Chuck Bell, Eastside AD Donald Buie and head coach Gator Hoskins to hear their thoughts on the ACSB's decision. Gainesville High, which doesn't have space on campus to build a stadium, declined to comment for this story.

Alachua County School Board OKs Citizens Field purchase, Buchholz stadium

Buchholz athletics excited for earned opportunity, unlocked potential

When Pankey took over as AD for Ron Brooks in May 2025, he quickly went to work to make an on-campus stadium a reality. It seemed unlikely, given that the construction of Citizens Field felt like a longshot. Adding another $16 million to the budget looked impossible.

"At some point, you have something in the community that's yours," Pankey said. "We're surprised and extremely thankful for the board that they're taking a commitment to athletics at Buchholz and in the community."

Pankey's background drove him to think outside the box. As the Bobcats wrestling coach who didn't attend BHS, he holds no special connection to Citizens Field that many in Gainesville do. He wanted what was best for the school, and that meant playing in a stadium at the school with the community behind them.

"I'm not knocking Citizens at all. We have a great partnership, and it brought a lot of value," Pankey said. "But the reality is that's 30-40 minutes from Buchholz kids and parents. There're issues with parking and being in a different area."

Momentum within the ACSB helped change the situation. The conflict over Citizens Field, and chairman Thomas Vu's desire to for each school to have their own stadium opened a door for the northwest Gainesville community to voice their opinion.

At a workshop in the morning and during public comment in the school board meeting Tuesday evening, many community members offered support for the stadium.

Buchholz football stars shine in second half to knock off Forest

That helped change the vote as both Janine Plavac and Leanetta McNealy – two yes votes – said they were reflecting community desires.

Outside of football, Pankey said the stadium allows for unleashed potential for other BHS sports. Soccer, lacrosse and flag football will no longer need to venture to Jonesville.

"Girls lacrosse had to pay to rent and practice at other areas. Boys and girls soccer practice on half fields. Flag football practices in a triangle," Pankey said. "This is going to benefit thousands of student athletes at Buchholz."

Bobcats football ready to defend their own turf

The construction of a new stadium is at a perfect time for BHS football. This decade, the Bobcats – with five consecutive regional championships – have become a state powerhouse.

"A lot of us longtime Buchholz guys never thought it would actually happen," Bell said. "Excited that all three schools are going to have the opportunity to play in a special place."

Bell called the process as fair and equitable as possible, given issues for a stadium at Eastside and the impracticability of one at GHS.

"From a Buchholz standpoint, we're excited to defend our turf and have a place we feel proud to play home games at," Bell said.

That wasn't the case at Citizens. With a field covered in sand and dirt, Bell said the City of Gainesville and Alachua County Public Schools were offering a bad introduction to some of the programs BHS welcomed – top teams in the state with recruits who hold offers from UF just four miles away.

"We were putting out dirty, ragged-out welcome mats," Bell said. "Being able to welcome people to Gainesville and Alachua County and show people we do things first class."

Santa Fe football powers past Eastside at Citizens Field. See our best photos!

Eastside football worried about competitive advantage

In a document detailing the results of a three-month study regarding the viability of each school having their own football stadium, the ACSB revealed that Eastside logically made the most sense. Construction would cause limited disruption due to EHS location and there is ample parking.

However, Eastside ended Tuesday without a stadium. Mosquito issues ultimately plagued the proposal.

AD Donald Buie, who is an EHS alum, understands the issues with mosquitos. He mentioned how JV games have been played at 6 p.m. to avoid problems. However, that shouldn't be enough to not grant Eastside a stadium.

"I don't want to step on my administrative toes too much, but if you're asking me personally, I'd love to see Eastside have their own stadium to keep up with the competitive advantage," Buie said.

That competitive advantage bothers Gator Hoskins as well. The Rams head coach worries Buchholz will benefit from a stadium with their logo on it.

"If I was a football player, it would feel good to walk out and see Rams painted in the endzone and a Ram logo at midfield," Hoskins said.

And just like how northwest Gainesville wants a stadium at Buchholz, the east side desires one at EHS – even if it isn't voiced as loudly.

"It's something the whole east side wants," Hoskins said.

A school board seat is on the November 3rd General Election ballot. Plavac is running against Hunter Miller for District 1. In a Facebook post last Wednesday, Miller said he doesn't support a new stadium for Buchholz.

articles.title: Will Michael Malone, UNC basketball prove ACC poll, rankings wrong? Here are predictions
articles.summary: Michael Malone's first UNC basketball team faces modest expectations as ACC voters and analytics project the Tar Heels outside the league's top tier.
articles.body:
UNC basketball isn't projected to be a championship-caliber team in the ACC during the 2026-27 season.

According to analytics sites and the official ACC preseason poll, which was released by the league on Oct. 13, the Tar Heels have been picked to finish fifth in the 18-team league.

Selected by a panel of regional and national media, the 2026-27 poll has Duke as the favorite to win a third straight conference championship. No Tar Heels were selected for the preseason All-ACC teams.

Entering its first season under coach Michael Malone , an NBA champion with the Denver Nuggets , UNC has 11 newcomers on its roster to join senior forward Jarin Stevenson, senior guard Jaydon Young and sophomore guard Isaiah Denis. Utah transfer Terrence Brown, Virginia Tech transfer Neo Avdalas, N.C. State transfer Matt Able, international center Sayon Keita and freshman Maximo Adams are among the talented players joining the Tar Heels.

ACC basketball preseason predictions, poll 2026-27 season

First-place votes in parentheses , followed by total points

Here are the preseason All-ACC first and second teams.

UNC basketball ranking in USA TODAY coaches poll, AP Top 25

The USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll and AP Top 25 haven't been released, but those national rankings will be revealed before the regular season starts on Nov. 1. The Tar Heels dropped out of the final coaches poll and AP Top 25 at the conclusion of the 2026 NCAA Tournament.

UNC debuted at No. 25 in the national polls ahead of the 2025-26 season, which was its lowest national ranking to start a season in 20 years. After winning the 2005 NCAA title, the Tar Heels entered the 2005-06 season unranked with a freshman class headlined by Tyler Hansbrough, Danny Green, Bobby Frasor and Marcus Ginyard. That team won 23 games and was eliminated in the second round of the 2006 NCAA Tournament.

UNC basketball ranking on KenPom, Bart Torvik, EvanMiya analytics sites

The analytic sites aren't high on Michael Malone and the Tar Heels in the 2026-27 season. As of Oct. 13, UNC is 37th in KenPom, projected to finish fifth in the ACC. The Heels are 50th on Evan Miyakawa's site, projected to finish sixth in the ACC, and 45th in Bart Torvik's T-Rank Rankings, predicted to finish eighth in the ACC.

Liverpool , hit hard by injuries during the international window, suffered a 3-0 defeat to Manchester City at Anfield on Sunday afternoon. They controlled the game until Ryan Gravenberch was controversially sent off, after which the visitors scored back-to-back goals. The Reds' lack of squad depth remains a concern; however, many of their youngsters are still on loan for regular minutes before they can stake a claim in Andoni Iraola's plans.

A comfortable outing for the teenage custodian, who was hardly threatened in their commanding 3-0 win against ten-man Kortrijk. The clean sheet should boost his confidence ahead of the weekend's Cup tie with Virton.

Was brought in as a late substitute in their thumping 5-1 win against Angers. Had a major opportunity to find the net in the dying minutes after being set up from close range by Noah Edjouma. Anthony Lopes made a sharp foot-save to deny the attacking prospect.

An error on his first full debut earned Sevilla an early lead. But the young centre-back overcame the initial setback and showed great mentality and composure before scoring a dramatic 100th-minute equaliser to salvage a 3–3 draw for Levante.

Although Hartberg snatched a narrow win over Austria Lustenau, the Hungarian struggled between the sticks, conceding three goals from just 1.68 xGOT. He must step up his game against league leaders Rapid Wien, with the Blue-Whites set to travel to Vienna for their next Bundesliga encounter.

Joel Bagan remains the preferred left-back, with Scanlon brought on as a late substitute in Cardiff City's 2-1 defeat to Blackburn Rovers.

Was taken off around the hour mark with Forest Green trailing 3-0.

Pulled off some close-range saves against Worcester to secure a clean sheet, but missed their recent encounters with Warrington Rylands and Ashton United due to an injury.

Has been rotated in goal for FC Cincinnati reserves in the MLS Next Pro – Eastern Conference. Returned to action this weekend after a few erroneous outings, but the Polish prospect had another disappointing day, conceding two late goals in their 1-2 setback.

Worked on his fitness during the break, and was once again deployed as a second-half substitute in their 2-2 draw with Racing Santander. Could not make any notable contribution while on the pitch.

articles.title: Louisville basketball picked 3rd in ACC preseason poll before Year 3 under Pat Kelsey
articles.summary: Louisville basketball was picked to finish Year 3 of the Pat Kelsey era third in the ACC standings. A look at the ACC preseason poll, awards.
articles.body:
Louisville basketball 's second trip through the ACC under Pat Kelsey was a letdown. The Cardinals finished sixth after coming in at No. 2 in the conference's preseason poll .

Will Kelsey and his overhauled roster bounce back in 2026-27? A select panel of 48 media members thinks so.

UofL was third in the ACC's predicted order of finish released Oct. 13.

For the fourth consecutive preseason, Duke was crowned the favorite to win the conference. The Blue Devils have swept its regular-season and tournament championships the past two years.

After going 18-2 in ACC play and reaching the conference tournament championship game in Year 1 under Kelsey, Louisville posted an 11-7 record and failed to advance past the tournament's quarterfinal round in 2025-26.

Some of the drop-off can be attributed to a back injury that sidelined star freshman point guard Mikel Brown Jr. from eight of the Cards' regular-season ACC games — including losses to Stanford, Duke and Virginia — in addition to the entire postseason. But the conference was also deeper than it was the year prior, doubling its NCAA Tournament bids from four to eight.

"If you can win this conference, you can win a national championship," Kelsey told reporters Oct. 6 at ACC Tipoff. "We're excited about competing for that."

UofL returns only one scholarship player from its 2025-26 roster, junior guard Adrian Wooley . Kelsey's collection of 11 newcomers, comprising eight veterans out of the NCAA transfer portal and three freshmen, ranks fifth on 247Sports' national leaderboard .

The centerpiece of Louisville's portal haul, former Kansas forward Flory Bidunga , earned first-team preseason All-ACC honors. The reigning Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year was the only Division I player to average more than 13 points, 8.5 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game in 2025-26.

Senior guard Jackson Shelstad , an Oregon transfer, appeared on the preseason All-ACC second team. He was on pace to post new career highs in points (15.6) and assists per game (4.9) before an injury to his shooting hard cut short his final season with the Ducks to 12 appearances.

After exhibitions against Kansas (Oct. 21) and Mercyhurst (Oct. 28), the Cards open the regular season Nov. 2 against Chattanooga at the KFC Yum Center . ACC play begins with a Dec. 30 trip to Virginia Tech.

articles.title: Panthers OT Taylor Moton details scary events that led to discovery of blood clots
articles.summary: Panthers OT Taylor Moton talked about the terrifying details that led to the discovery of his blood clots earlier this year.
articles.body:
On Tuesday, Carolina Panthers offensive tackle Taylor Moton broke down the team's huddle to cap off his first practice of the 2026 campaign. And in almost any another season, that probably wouldn't have been too big of a deal.

But it was this afternoon, as the 32-year-old returned to the field after spending the past handful of months recovering from blood clots. After the session, Moton spoke about the terrifying details that led to the discovery of the issue.

Moton, running back Trevor Etienne and defensive lineman Tershawn Wharton were all officially designated to return to practice earlier in the day. While their respective statuses for Sunday's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles remain unclear, head coach Dave Canales seemed encouraged by what he saw.

"They all looked pretty good today," Canales told reporters . "We have to see how they respond to today's physical practice, and they all got a good, significant amount of reps. That was the plan.

"As you can imagine, there's a ramp-up, training part of it—getting their body right. They're in great shape. Football shape's different. This is a collision sport, not a contact sport. So, wanted to see how their bodies respond to a physical, padded practice before we make any decisions."

With Moton sidelined, the Panthers started 2026 first-round pick Monroe Freeling at right tackle for the first four games of the season. Freeling's outlook for Week 6 isn't exactly certain either, as the rookie has been dealing with a knee injury coming off the win over the Detroit Lions.

articles.title: Iowa women's basketball guards are ready for whatever role they may fill
articles.summary: Iowa women's basketball team has six players listed as guards. Each of them is ready to start or come off the bench and do their part.
articles.body:
IOWA CITY — One of the biggest talking points heading into Iowa women's basketball season is that the Hawkeyes have fewer players on the roster but a lot of options at the guard position.

Head coach Jan Jensen's squad has six guards: Taylor Stremlow, Dani Carnegie, Journey Houston, Chit-Chat Wright, Amari Whiting and Bria Medina. Jocelyn Faison is listed as a guard/forward.

Assuming that All-Big Ten preseason team player Ava Heiden starts at center and Wright retains her starting spot, that would leave three other spots in the starting lineup.

Carnegie was a unanimous All-SEC pick at Georgia last season after averaging 17.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game.

Stremlow started 18 games for the Hawkeyes last season and averaged 7.9 points and 4.3 assists per contest.

Whiting started all 34 games for Oklahoma State in 2025-26 and was top 20 in the Big 12 in steals and rebounds.

Houston had an impressive freshman campaign for Iowa, averaging 5.4 points and 5.1 rebounds in just 15.6 minutes per game.

Medina scored 23.6 points per game at Knox College, the second-highest average in Division III.

Instead of it seeming like a competition, Stremlow, Carnegie, Houston, Whiting and Medina are all ready to embrace whatever role is asked of them.

"That's the ticket," Jensen said in her press conference at women's basketball media day on Oct. 13. "Is when your time comes, from when you come off the bench or you start, is 'What can I do when I'm there?'"

The players are ready for whatever role they will play this season

Houston is making the transition from forward to guard, and Jensen has said a lot about how good of a summer she has had in the offseason. She said Houston's defense has improved and she's been developing her shot. The second-year Hawkeye just wants the chance to play her role.

"Knowing my role, we have plenty of scorers," Houston said. "We got Dani, Chat and Ava, so, just hit shots when I'm open and just try to get them open."

In terms of wanting to be a starter, Houston noted that she thinks everyone at this level wants to be one, but she will take whatever is given to her.

"If that means coming off the bench, coming off the bench, and I'm going to give it my all," Houston said.

Stremlow is a captain this season, as voted by her teammates, along with Heiden and Wright. She thinks the deep roster is a good thing, knowing that whoever is out on the court is going to do their best.

"I think whoever's on the floor is going to be a threat," Stremlow said. "especially with Ava (Heiden) inside and the attention that she demands in the post. If people want to double down on her and make them pay on the outside and if people want to step over the line, we'll make them pay on the inside, so I think it's pretty exciting."

Whiting is a transfer from Oklahoma State by way of BYU and has played almost 100 collegiate games. In terms of the role she would hope to play, she said, "whatever coach wants."

"Whoever comes off the bench is just as good as who's starting," Whiting said. "So I'm really excited. I think all of us just really want the best for each other and to be the best versions of ourselves."

With the smaller roster (11 players), there is a hope to spread out minutes more than in years past.

"As fast as we want to play offensively, and then as hard as we expect them to play on the defensive end, we are going to need to have a few more rest periods," assistant coach Abby Stamp said.

Stamp gave an example from last season, saying that Wright was averaging 35 minutes a game for the Hawkeyes, and that might have been a little too high.

"We have seen a lot of good things from our guards so far throughout the summer and then into now," Stamp added. "For us, we just want to just make sure that we're taking care of the ball, we're getting high-percentage shots, and then we're doing everything fundamentally sound on the defensive end."

The expectation is to not have much of a drop-off from whoever the starters are to whoever comes off the bench. Jensen has talked a lot about the team being "other-centered." Stamp said that the "we-over-me" mentality has quickly become a trademark of the Hawkeye program.

"I think that is definitely Jan's character," Stamp said. "Jan is very, very other-centered and trying to lift up the person around you. I think that's what we want to have with our group, day in and day out, year in and year out."

articles.title: Capitals' Alex Ovechkin Jokingly Gifted Forklift By Hurricanes Ahead of NHL Retirement in Photo
articles.summary: The Carolina Hurricanes apparently gave Washington Capitals star Alex Ovechkin a send-off to remember ahead of his last regular-season game at Lenovo Center.
articles.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes apparently gave Washington Capitals star Alex Ovechkin a send-off to remember ahead of his last regular-season game at Lenovo Center.

The Capitals shared a photograph of Ovechkin sitting in a forklift ahead of a Tuesday night matchup against the Canes.

"Kind gesture here, as the Canes have gifted Ovi a forklift as part of his farewell tour," the photo caption read.

Can Rangers Survive Without Shesterkin? 😓

The Hurricanes (5-1-1) and Capitals (3-2) dropped the puck in Raleigh at 6:45 p.m. ET.

Ovechkin contributed an assist back when the Capitals opened the season in Raleigh with a 5-2 loss on Oct. 2.

He scored his first goal of the campaign in the Caps' most recent game, a 5-3 Sunday loss to the Seattle Kraken.

Tuesday marks the first time this season Ovechkin, who announced earlier this month he would be retiring after the 2026-27 season, will be playing in an opponent's arena for the last time in his regular-season career.

That could mean a season full of tributes honoring an NHL career during which Ovechkin broke Wayne Gretzky's all-time goalscoring record.

Recently-retired Los Angeles Kings star Anže Kopitar, for instance, was celebrated with postgame handshake lines during his final NHL season.

The Daily Faceoff's Jeff Marek speculated on a recent episode of Daily Faceoff Live how the Hurricanes celebrate Ovechkin's career could set the tone for what his retirement tour will look like around the NHL this season.

That likely won't be the Capitals' focus heading into Tuesday's Metropolitan matchup. A division win over the defending Stanley Cup champions could would mark a valuable two points for a team hoping to make a final playoff run with Ovechkin next spring.

articles.title: WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights From October 13
articles.summary: As WWE NXT continued to set the stage for Halloween Havoc, the October 13 show included a massive No. 1 contender battle between Tony D'Angelo and Myles Borne.
articles.body:
As WWE NXT continued to set the stage for Halloween Havoc, the October 13 show included a massive No. 1 contender battle between Tony D'Angelo and Myles Borne.

Continuing the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic, Fraxiom collided with Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno, and The Vanity Project faced the underdog duo of Chazz "Starboy" Hall and Mini Vikingo.

Tristan Angels and Saquon Shugars also looked to settle their issues in the ring. Wren Sinclair appeared after her shocking battle royal win last week.

For live grades, highlights and full results for NXT, keep reading below.

Dusty Tag Team Classic: The Vanity Project vs. Chazz "Starboy" Hall and Mini Vikingo

Last Time in Action: Chazz "Starboy" Hall and Mini Vikingo defeated BirthRight to advance in the Dusty Classic (NXT, September 29); Ricky Smokes and Brad Baylor defeated Cruz Montana and EK Prosper (NXT, September 15).

Starboy caused problems for Smokes early, but it was a hot tag to Vikingo that truly caused problems for The Vanity Project.

They took over the ring until Myka Lockwood distracted them, allowing Smokes and Baylor to lay out the underdog team into the first Picture-in-Picture break.

Out of the break, Vikingo laid out Baylor with a Spanish Fly, forcing both men to tag in their partners. Hall laid into the champion including a Double Pele Kick then a Slice Bread and Standing Shooting Star on Smokes.

Smokes kicked out after a Springboard 450 Splash. Hall DDTed Baylor into a 630 Splash from Vikingo, but Smokes broke up the pin attempt.

Smokes got his knees up against a diving Starboy and followed up with Hit and Quit It for the victory.

Hall and Vikingo looked great throughout with unreal athleticism on display, but as this match went on, it became increasingly clear that the underdogs had no chance.

They hit the champions with everything in their arsenal, only to fall fairly easily at the end to the champions' finishing move despite them fighting from behind throughout.

The ultimate goal was to say that Vanity Project were just too good for the underdogs to take down, but the action said it was the champions that could not keep up with the new team.

Vanity Project needed to win at least once as the current NXT tag team champions, but hopefully they will get more actively involved in their semifinal battle.

Baylor and Smokes def. Hall and Vikingo by pinfall to advance to the semifinals of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic.

The show started with a recap of last week's main event.

While Booker T praised Vikingo, he also called out that his offense was not as effective due to his size.

The praise for Starboy as a representative of the WWE ID Program did not land when so many have recently left that program, including one of Starboy's primary rivals in EVOLVE, Cappuccino Jones.

Last Time in Action: Saquon Shugars alongside Tony D'Angelo lost to Mason Rook for an NXT Championship opportunity (NXT, September 15); Tristan Angels lost to Zilla Fatu (NXT, September 1).

Shugars wanted to get his hands on Angels immediately and backed up his words with action once the bell rang.

He had Angels reeling, caused him to toss steel chairs into the ring into the commercial break.

Angels tricked Shugars during the break and took over the action. Guided by the support of the crowd, Shugars fought free of multiple submission attempts to fight back.

Shugars went for a Moonsault but hesitated due to the pain in his jaw, allowing Angels to duck it. Angels then caught Shugars with a Knee Drop Bulldog for the victory.

This was ugly action that came off fully as two green stars struggling to keep the pace. It got worse down the stretch as nothing seemed to land.

Both men have charisma to spare, but both have had struggles like this early in their NXT solo runs. Shugars was not hitting his offense clean.

The worst though was the struggle of Angels to hit his finishing move, leading to a flat and unimpressive finish.

It all looked so bad that NXT did not replay anything from the finish of the contest and quickly tried to shift the focus to the next segment.

If this was supposed to show that Shugars is only a couple steps away from challenging for the NXT Championship, it was a colossal failure.

Given Angels' frequent attempts to cheat to survive this match, this is only the beginning of this rivalry. Hopefully they will learn from the first failing.

Before heading out for his match, Sugars promised to go for gold after taking down Angels. Grayson Waller arrived to warn Shugars he is not ready.

Shugars walking out of the interview trash-talking his way into his entrance was a great visual and should be replicated in his future entrances.

Wren Sinclair Officially Gets the Shot at Kelani Jordan at Halloween Havoc

Wren Sinclair explained that she was no longer scared to take risks. She was stepping up for herself and Kendal Grey in seeking out the NXT Women's Championship.

Kelani Jordan interrupted to declare that she refused to face Wren since she manipulated her way to this opportunity, offering to face Kali Armstrong, anyone from TNA or the real Lady Shani.

Robert Stone arrived and asked the crowd what they wanted, officially announcing that Lani would defend against Wren at Halloween Havoc.

This was a long segment to only confirm the inevitable match that was set up last week.

Wren struggled with her words more than usual, leaving Lani looking like the far more confident promo in comparison.

This was especially rough when Wren took some heel-like shortcuts to get to this spot, while Lani made the best points despite speaking as the cowardly heel.

Stone continues to be a wishy-washy general manager whose decisions are driven by whoever he spoke to last, which makes for a terrible authority figure.

Izzi Dame explained to Niko Vance in an awkward pre-tape that she wanted to figure out Zaria and show everyone her flaws.

Wren still did not truly explain why she stole Shani's spot and mask beyond a half-hearted apology.

Stone and Wren also never truly explained what happened to her suspension.

Kelani put her hair down for this appearance, showing off her new long blonde flowy hair.

Cruz Montana encouraged Lizzy Rain before he got a call from his mother. Dion Lennox then laid out Montana and re-called his mother, promising to send him back to a dark place.

Reina de Reinas Championship: La Catalina (c) vs. Kali Armstrong

Last Time in Action: La Catalina and Kali Armstrong both lost in the No. 1 contender battle royal (NXT, October 6).

Catalina danced around Kali early in this contest, but that only angered the challenger, who exposed the cement under the padding on the floor.

The Reina de Reinas champion fought back with a Senton off the steel steps to send the match to a PIP break.

Catalina tried to run around the strikes of Kali, but the challenger continued to show the danger behind her strong strikes.

Kali went for the Kali Connection, but Catalina knocked her to the floor onto the exposed cement followed by a Shining Wizard to retain the Reina de Reinas Championship.

It was certainly a choice to deliver just one women's match over two hours when NXT's women's division is so far ahead of the men's, but at least the one match was good.

Kali especially drove the action, but the two had obvious chemistry from the jump. The match flowed with solid drama to sell the possible title change.

The finish did not fully land, especially the telegraphed cement bump that is both overly dangerous and looked ineffective on camera, but this was overall a strong showcase of two rising stars.

Before long, NXT will need to strap up Kali, who works every match like she is already the champion, which makes it hard to see her losing so many big opportunities.

Catalina def. Kali by pinfall to retain the AAA Reina de Reinas Championship.

Catalina has a solid flow to her offense, but she needs to find more impactful signature offense. She cannot just rely on Headscissors.

Kali went to Robert Stone's office to complain about last week, and Stone announced that he got approval for her to challenge Catalina.

Wren Sinclair ran into Myles Borne backstage and called him selfish. Kendal Grey arrived to announce she was cleared, and she and Wren start strategizing.

EK Prosper found Chazz "Starboy" Hall and Mini Vikingo and encouraged them. The Vanity Project mocked them, and the trios agreed to fight next week.

articles.title: Panic in Dallas: Cowboys defense holds emergency summit as season spirals after Bucs loss
articles.summary: DeMarvion Overshown reveals details of the Dallas Cowboys' defensive players-only meeting after surrendering 241 rushing yards to Tampa Bay.
articles.body: Five weeks into the season and fresh off an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Dallas Cowboys are already breaking out the oldest crisis gimmick in football: the defensive players-only meeting. Sitting at 2-3 and watching their defense get pushed around on a weekly basis, the entire unit gathered behind closed doors on Monday morning to air out their issues. Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown described the session as a blunt "heart-to-heart." "Looking ourselves in the mirror," Overshown said. "Putting what we wanted our standard to be, we put that on the board. We went by bullet point, bullet point. Are we holding up to this? Are we being this? As a unit, how can we get closer? What is it? Just hearing from all of us. It really wasn't like a fire drill conversation, it was more so, 'What can I do to help you? What do I expect from you on Sundays, or every Monday walk throughs?' We've got to talk to each other like that because the ship is only going to go as far as the weakest person on the boat. As long as we all in this together, I think we're going to be great. I know we're going to be there." JERRY JONES SLAMS TABLE AFTER DAK PRESCOTT THROWS CRITICAL LATE INTERCEPTION IN BRUTAL COWBOYS LOSS Writing bullet points on a dry-erase board is cute, but it does not erase what happened against Tampa Bay. Dallas got thoroughly embarrassed at home by a winless Buccaneers squad, surrendering 241 rushing yards and making an 0-4 offense look explosive. The Cowboys surrendered 419 total yards, blew basic run fits, and failed to force a single takeaway. Through five weeks, Dallas has surrendered at least 375 yards every game. Management is now scrambling to stop the bleeding before a tough road trip to Green Bay. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Defensive coordinator Christian Parker is moving upstairs to the coaching booth, and longtime NFL coach Mike Pettine was hired as a senior assistant to provide adult supervision. Meanwhile, Dallas hopes Overshown's return from a four-game hamstring injury adds badly needed speed. Whiteboard therapy is fine, but unless this group starts tackling someone, the Cowboys' season is officially cooked. articles.body:
Tuesday, October 13, is an important day in the National Hockey League due to it being Frozen Frenzy Day!!

The Frozen Frenzy is an annual day (early) on the NHL schedule in which all 32 NHL teams lace up their skates and are slated for a game.

For the Colorado Avalanche, they will take on the Dallas Stars (on the road) in a Tuesday evening showdown.

The Avalanche will attempt to capture a victory without their top defenceman, Cale Makar, who is absent from the team due to a major family moment.

The reason Cale Makar is away from the Colorado Avalanche right now is that his wife is giving birth.

"Cale Makar's wife is due any moment so he will not he playing tonight, Avs team spokesman says."

His wife is actually expecting twins , so Makar will have double trouble on his hands over the next few months at home.

"Makar, 28, has been his typically dynamic self to start this season, as he's put up three goals anf four assists for seven points in five games played while averaging 21 and a half minutes of ice time. Last season, the Calgary native scored 20 goals and added 59 assists for 79 points in 75 games, finishing second in voting for the Norris Trophy. He also served as an alternate captain for the Canadian men's national team at the 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Olympics in February, putting up two goals and four assists for six points in six games en route to Canada earning a silver medal."

The Avalanche X account also announced the Makar news:

"Cale Makar will not be in the lineup tonight. He is back in Denver with his wife awaiting the arrival of their twins. Wishing all the best to the Makar family during this exciting time!"

The UFC welterweight division likely has a new tallest fighter.

Meet Luis Francischinelli. A 6-foot-6 welterweight with an 80-inch reach. He's a unique challenge, which is what Will Rentz found out the hard way Tuesday at Dana White's Contender Series 96 .

articles.title: Red Wings earn a point, but lose in overtime to Devils 5-4
articles.summary: The Red Wings may have found a new, explosive scoring line Tuesday, Oct. 13, but it wasn't enough to earn a victory.
articles.body:
DETROIT - The Red Wings may have found a new, explosive scoring line Tuesday, October 13, but it wasn't enough to earn a victory.

Jack Hughes scored at 1 minute 19 seconds of overtime, giving New Jersey a 5-4 victory.

Jesper Bratt found Hughes streaking down the middle of the ice, and Hughes scored on the breakaway on goaltender John GIbson.

Alex DeBrincat scored his second of the game, and fourth on the season, tying the game 4-4 at 5:46 of the third period. DeBrincat one-timed a pass from Moritz Seider, who found open ice in the zone and found DeBrincat alone near the dot.

The line of Emmitt Finnie centering Alex DeBrincat and Michael Brandegg-Nygard had a dominant evening. DeBrincat had two goals and an assist, while Finnie and Brandsegg-Nygard each had a goal and assist.

The Devils (3-3-0) outshot the Wings (1-3-2) 37-26

Jesper Bratt's goal at 16:52 of the second period broke a 3-3 tie during a wild, back and forth period. Bratt lifted a shot from the high slot that got past screened Gibson.

Gibson made a huge save on Arseny Gritsyuk off a 2-on-1 rush that kept the game 4-4 near the midway point of the third period.

Evan Rodrigues, Anthony Mantha, Nico Hischier (power play) and Jesper Bratt had Devils goals.

Trailing 1-0, the Wings tied it on Finnie's second goal at 18:35 of the first period on a blast from the left dot after getting an outlet pass from Brandsegg-Nygard. Finnie returned the favor at 1:43 of the second period, setting up Brandsegg-Nygard on a 2-on-1 rush, Brandsegg-Nygard one-timing pass for his second goal.

But Mantha -the former Wing scored his first in New Jersey - and Hischier scored, putting the Devils ahead 3-2, before DeBrincat tied the game with his third goal, from the high slot at 15:10.

articles.title: Ohio State’s reshuffled right side to meet Indiana’s sack leaders in a top-5 showdown

articles.body:
COLUMBUS, Ohio (AP) — The line of scrimmage figures to be an area of focus Saturday when No. 4 Ohio State visits No. 5 Indiana.

That is typically true of any high-profile Big Ten game, but the topic was of even more interest as the week began because the Buckeyes have uncertainty at multiple offensive line positions as they prepare for a rematch of last season's conference title game.

Senior lineman Austin Siereveld missed Ohio State's win over Maryland on Saturday with an illness, and coach Ryan Day labeled him as day-to-day.

That led to a reshuffled front with sophomore Jake Cook entering the lineup at right guard and junior Gabe VanSickle taking over at right tackle.

VanSickle had already been starting since Phillip Daniels was injured in the Buckeyes' second game of the season at Texas, but he was at right guard while Siereveld took Daniels' place at right tackle for the subsequent three games.

Day offered no update on Siereveld on Tuesday, but he said Daniels is expected to practice in full this week.

That could mean he returns to right tackle with VanSickle at right guard if Siereveld remains out, but Day said the staff was satisfied with what it saw from VanSickle against the Terrapins.

Ohio State allowed two sacks, but the Buckeyes ran for 207 yards, their most since they had 237 in the season opener against Ball State.

"I thought for short notice being able to step in like that, it wasn't all perfect, but there was a lot of good out there," Day said. "So now we'll be able to move him around if we need to a little bit in practice more, we'll move him back down to guard and we'll fill the right tackle and see how the week goes."

Regardless of who starts, the Buckeyes figure to have their hands full with an Indiana defensive front that is among the best in the nation.

Ohio State is 14th in the Big Ten and 75th in the country in sacks allowed (1.83 per game) while ranking 11th and 57th, respectively, in tackles for loss allowed per game (5.0). The Hoosiers lead the Big Ten and rank in the top eight nationally in both categories.

Indiana defensive ends Stephen Daley and Tobi Osunsanmi have five sacks apiece, while tackles Tyrique Tucker and Marion Landino have combined for three more.

While Osunsanmi is a transfer from Kansas State, the other three were part of a unit that was key to Indiana's 13-10 win over Ohio State in last season's Big Ten title game, in which Julian Sayin was sacked five times and the Buckeyes finished with 58 yards rushing.

"It is going to be a huge challenge," Day said. "They do an excellent job up front on defense. Their defensive line is one of the biggest challenges we'll have all season, so we've got to have a great week of preparation."

Indiana native Ian Moore is a new starter at left tackle for the Buckeyes, while seniors Luke Montgomery and Carson Hinzman both started against the Hoosiers last season along with Siereveld and Daniels.

Tegra Tshabola started at right guard but was injured during the game and replaced by VanSickle.

"The good news is some of these guys have played against Indiana before, so they know how good these guys are and what comes with it," Day said. "So they're going to have all of our attention for sure."

articles.title: Mile posts: Items on Trace Obbink, Addison Liston, Gavin Grunhovd, Biya Simbassa, Camryn Sattler, Clare Stahr
articles.summary: The Le Mars Community grad sparked the Dordt men to the Gold division title with 49 points.
articles.body:
Junior Trace Obbink looks like he might be the undisputed leader of the Dordt University men's cross country team.

The Le Mars Community grad pulled away over the final 1,000 meters to secure his first college win at the Holiday Inn Express Classic hosted by the Defenders on Saturday, Oct. 10. Obbink covered the flat 8-kilometer course at Dordt in Sioux Center in 24 minutes, 57.6 seconds, missing his personal record by less than 10 seconds, to spark the Defenders to the Gold division title with 49 points.

Track Obbink had a great day, securing the first win of his collegiate career," Dordt coach Nate Wolf said. "The depth of the team was apparent as several athletes traded positions within the scoring five and seven from earlier races this season."

Obbink leads off this edition of the WEEKEND UPDATE of the best performances by Iowa-based collegiate and post collegiate distance runners and triathletes.

Obbink has been on a tear this fall, first knocking more than a minute off his previous 8K best set in 2025 while taking 16th place at the Augustana University Invitational on Sept. 25. Obbink ran 24:48.2 that day and was the second Defenders runner over the finish line. On Saturday, Obbink pulled away from Northwestern College sophomore standout Caleb Tofteland to win by 18.7 seconds. Sophomore Hudson Hamilton was the next Dordt finisher in seventh in 25:29.6.

Obbink's junior teammate Brett Gifford, who prepped at Dowling Catholic, was the No. 5 scorer for Dordt in 16th place. Gifford ran 26:00.9 as Doane was a distant second in the team race with 81 points. Northwestern junior and North Polk product Alik McIlravy was the sixth-place team's No. 2 finisher in 26th place in 26:30.4. Next to finish was Dordt senior Caleb Van Beek in 26:32.2. Van Beek attended Western Christian (Hull). He was followed by freshman teammate Tyler Rozenboom, an ex-Unity Christian (Orange City) runner, in 28th place in 26:32.4.

Another Dordt athlete nearly made it a double victory for Iowa natives in the women's 6K Gold race. Sophomore Addison Liston was edged for the win by sophomore teammate Joy Koole by 1.8 seconds. Liston, another Unity Christian grad, ran 22:17.4 for second as the champion and top-ranked (in NAIA) Defenders rolled to the team title with just 25 points.

Helping to break up the Dordt juggernaut at the top was Northwestern College senior Emily DeGroot. DeGroot, who prepped at MOC-FV (Orange City), was fourth in 22:20.6 to help the Red Raiders secure seventh in the team race. Northwestern also had a top-10 finisher in senior Kayden Spencer, a former Ogden and Des Moines Area Community College runner. Spencer secured 10th in 22:44.8.

Dordt senior and Waukee High grad Isabella Webb was the No. 6 finisher for the Defenders in 13th place in 22:52.0. Freshman teammate Katie Young, another Unity Christian product, was 18th in 23:02.2. Dordt sophomore Elyse Zwart, who attended Boyden-Hull, claimed 20th in 23:04.6. The leader for Morningside University was sophomore and ex-Cherokee Washington prep Estefana Beisswenger in 26th place in 23:16.5.

In the men's 8K Black competition, former Iowa City West and Iowa Central Community College athlete Seth Cheney took the victory. The Fitness Sports Distance Project athlete ran 26:08.2 to win by 31.8 seconds.

Continuing with the small colleges and the Indian Hills Invitational at Cedar Creek Golf Course in Ottumwa on Oct. 9. Mount Mercy University All-American Abby Knepper dominated the women's 5K competition, averaging 5:53 while running 18:17.7. The senior who competed for Beckman (Dyersville) won by nearly 45 seconds.

Helping the Mustangs take the team title with 55 points, the same as runner-up Indian Hills, was senior Kalin Rotzoll. The Clear Creek-Amana grad ran 19:05.6 for third place. The run of former Iowa preps continued with North Central (Manly) product Claire Rye finishing fourth in 19:24.8. Rye is a sophomore at William Penn. St. Ambrose senior Kaitlyn was the leader for fifth-place St. Ambrose (133 points) in fifth in 19:34.4. Former Mount Vernon-Lisbon runner Lourdes Mason, now a junior at Mount Mercy, was next to finish in 19:35.0. Third-place Des Moines Area Community College (80) was paced by eighth-place Addy Tesch in 19:46.4. Tesch ran for Ridge View (Holstein). The top 10 was rounded out by DMACC freshman and former Greene County (Jefferson) prep Kaycee Pittman in 19:55.5.

North Iowa Area Community Collee sophomore Gavin Grunhovd continued his run of excellent races by topping everyone in the 8K race. The North Iowa (Buffalo Center) grad ran 25:27.7 to top DMACC sophomore Sam Mora, a Dallas Center-Grimes product, by 26.3 seconds. Mora ran a new PR.

Mount Mercy's run to the team title with 42 points, 18 ahead of Indian Hills, started with sophomore Jack Stamp's fifth-place finish in 26:43.4. Stamp competed for Anamosa. Sophomore teammate Noah Gregoire, an ex-Liberty High runner, was next to finish in 27:02.0. The Mustangs' run continued with freshman and ex-Cedar Rapids Prairie prep in seventh in 27:04.3. Maquoketa Valley grad Matthaw Schaul, a Mount Mercy sophomore, was eighth in 27:12.8. He was just 2.2 seconds ahead of DMACC freshman and former Bondurant-Farrar athlete Brady Sanger in ninth. DMACC was third with 70 points.

Moving to the roads and the warm Chicago Marathon on Oct. 11. Former Sioux City North and Iowa Central runner Biya Simbassa, now an Asics athlete, finished 24th in the men's professional competition in 2:11:22. The Flagstaff, Arizona, resident ran the first half in 1:03:01. Drake University record-holder Reed Fischer of the Tinman Elite squad in Colorado took 31st among the men in 2:14:32. He ran the first half in 1:05:51. FSDP's Cody Baele of Des Moines accepted 47th in 2:18:08. Running Wild Elite's Joe Langridge took 51st among the men in 2:18:51. Langridge ran for Augustana College in Rock Island, Illinois.

Former Wartburg College and Cedar Rapids Kennedy runner Jacob Green grabbed 72nd among the men in 2:22:05. Former Iowa State runner Milo Greder was 95th in 2:24:00. Driftless Distance Project athlete Michael Goodenbour, who prepped at Cedar Falls before competing for Wartburg, was 159th in 2:28:52. Taking 202nd in the men's competition was former Des Moines Christian prep Jacob Fopma in 2:30:41. Crown Running's Michael Eyres, an ex-Luther College runner, was 592nd in 2:39:34. Kenyan Amos Kipruto blazed to the victory in 2:01:09.

Shifting to triathlon and the Ironman World Championships at Kailua-Kona, Hawaii, on Oct. 10, where former Buena Vista athlete and professor Matt Hanson finished 20th in the men's competition. The five-time Ironman event winner from Castle Rock, Colorado, was the third-best American after finishing the 2.4-mile swim in 54:50, the 112-mile bike in 4:36:11 and the 26.2-mile run in 2:40:34. His total time was 8:16:19.

"Not how I wanted the day to end up," Hanson wrote on Instagram. "But considering how poorly the race started, I'm happy to salvage a respectable result."

Hanson finished ninth in the final Ironman Pro Series. The winner was France's Vincent Luis in 7:47:27, who held off Norway's Gustav Iden by 1:36.

Moving back to cross country and the always competitive Nuttycombe Invitational hosted by Wisconsin at the Thomas Zimmer Championship Cross Country Course in Madison on Oct. 9. Arkansas finished fourth in the team race with 208 points and redshirt junior Allen Bonnesen was the Razorbacks' No. 4 finisher in 65th place in 23:36.6., a 4:45 pace per mile. Bonnesen started his career at Danville-New London and Iowa State before transferring to Fayetteville.

Former Iowa City High prep Ford Washburn was the No. 3 finisher and 83rd place for 13th-place Northern Arizona. The senior was timed in 23:47.9. Iowa State's final scorer was true freshman and ex-Cedar Falls High athlete Jaden Merrick in 140th place. Merrick ran 24:08.8 in his first college race at 8K. The Cyclones were only 19th in the team competition.

New Mexico took the team crown with 59 points and Colorado freshman Meshack Kipruto was the winner in 22:30.1.

Two Iowa distance running legends competed for champion Oregon at the Bill Dellinger Invitational in Springfield, Oregon, on Oct. 9. Iowa all-time 5K cross country record-holder Quentin Nauman picked up 26th place for the Ducks in 24:36.8. The Western Dubuque grad was not one of the scorers for Oregon, which scored 28 points and secured the team title with 28 points, 16 ahead of Weber State. Nauman made his college debut with a 52nd-place effort at the Cowboy Jamboree in Stillwater, Oklahoma, on Sept. 26.

Making his college debut, however, was Des Moines Christian great Caleb Ten Pas. The Oregon true freshman ran 25:20.4 for 55th place. The individual winner was Oregon star Simeon Birnbaum in 23:05.5.

Former Clinton High runner Camryn Sattler served as the No. 2 finisher for champion Tampa at the FSU Invitational at Apalachee Regional Park in Tallahassee, Florida, on Oct. 9. The Tampa junior who started her career at Iowa State covered the 6K course in 22:08.3 for fifth overall. That time is about 15 seconds off her PR. Tampa won the team crown with 37 points, nine of ahead of Jacksonville State.

Gilbert grad Clare Stahr earned the individual victory at the Brian T. Simpson Invitational on Gans Creek in Columbia, Missouri, on Oct. 10. The Truman State junior covered the 5K in a new PR of 18:17.1 while holding off Central Missouri sophomore Jordyn Brown by 1.5 seconds. Truman captured the team crown with 26 points, 25 ahead of host Central Missouri, while putting five runners in the top 10.

articles.title: Todd Beamer, Hazen varsity football seasons end early amid player shortages
articles.summary: Two Washington high school football programs, Todd Beamer and Hazen High School, are ending their varsity seasons early.
articles.body:
Two Washington high school football programs, Todd Beamer and Hazen High School, are ending their varsity seasons early.

Both school districts and coaches determined they no longer have enough players to safely field their teams. Officials at both schools cited player availability and safety concerns.

Todd Beamer Head Football Coach Rodney McCurry said his team has lost a significant portion of its roster to season-ending injuries.

"We just don't want to put our young guys out there to get hurt," McCurry said.

McCurry said coaches evaluated the health of their roster, as injuries continued to mount throughout the season.

"We took a hard look at our health, and we were rapidly having season-ending injuries every game," McCurry said.

Hazen High School is facing a similar situation. In a letter sent by the school's principal, officials attributed the decision to injuries, attrition, and academic suspensions.

Andy Barnes with the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association said individual schools and leagues are best positioned to evaluate their circumstances.

"They know what's going on in their communities and their schools and have to deal with all of that in the league," Barnes said.

While the teams' regular varsity seasons are ending early, football is not necessarily over for their players.

The WIAA said both schools are looking at playing exhibition junior varsity games and potentially scheduling varsity games against smaller schools at the 2A and 1A levels.

"I'm glad they are able to continue that process and will continue to work with the schools to help them navigate this," Barnes said.

Todd Beamer and Hazen are also expected to take the field against each other Friday at Renton Memorial Stadium.

"We're going to line up with Hazen and give our best, and they're going to give their best, and it's going to be a great football game," McCurry said.

For McCurry, the challenges his players have faced this season also provide a lesson that extends beyond football.

"We have to adapt and that is what we want to show our kids, that a little adversity in a positive manner is just how you live life," McCurry said.

articles.body:
Springfield head coach Chris Wallace was excited to be in attendance.

Getting to hear his team be announced Tuesday, Oct. 13, alongside other prominent state and national basketball programs as a participant in the upcoming 24th annual Flyin' To The Hoop event at Trent Arena left the first-year head coach all smiles about the state of his team.

"We're not a flash in the pan team. We got some great freshman and great sophomores, and it's the sophomores that are going to really contribute," Wallace said. "We are going to be a tough out, and we're going to be exciting to watch. I think Springfield basketball is definitely back."

The Wildcats will be one of 30 teams playing at FTTH this season. It will be Springfield's first appearance since 2020.

Other Dayton-area teams selected to play are Alter, Bellbrook, Centerville, Chaminade Julienne, Fairmont, Northridge, Valley View and Wayne.

The four-day event will be held as typical during Martin Luther King Holiday weekend from Jan. 15-18, 2027.

Bellbrook, Centerville, Fairmont are matched with some of the top teams coming in from out of state. Alter and CJ will play a Greater Catholic League Co-Ed game against one another. Northridge, Valley View and Wayne get to test themselves against other outstanding teams from Ohio.

As of Tuesday's announcement, there are six 5-star prospects and 29 others rated as 4-stars that will appear at FTTH. Asa Montgomery, a 5-star committed to Duke that plays at Hillgrove (Ga.), is ranked eighth overall in the 247Sports composite rankings for the class of 2027 and is the highest-rated recruit in the country set to appear.

Other notable recruits set to play are Pickerington Central's Landon Evans, a 3-star who committed to Wright State in July, and Xavier-commit Brandon Mason Jr., a 4-star who plays at Link Academy (Mo.)

The schedule will follow similar trends as used in recent years.

The Friday night slate has several national teams featuring multiple top prospects. Local teams begin Saturday and are interspersed with matchups against Ohio and other national teams. The event concludes Monday with host Fairmont's game and a small school showcase.

"We're going to have 11 of the top-20 Ohio teams regardless of their division," FTTH president Eric Horstman said. "We're going to have some of the top national teams. There's some stories behind some of them, there is a reason why you see these. You might not recognize the name right away, but there's a reason why they're coming to this event."

Centerville will be making its 21st appearance at FTTH. The Elks have participated more than any other school. Wayne is next on the list and is back on the schedule for the 20th consecutive event.

"When we show up, everything is first class. The way you're treated, the way the players are treated, how organized everything is, everything stays on time," Wayne head coach Nathan Martindale said. "We truly believe this is the number one showcase event in the country."

The 2027 event will be the first time Flyin' To The Hoop utilizes a shot clock for all contests. The move was approved by the Ohio High School Basketball Coaches Association in August and joins a list of 19 events in Ohio allowed to have a shot clock.

Two teams from the Nike EYBL Scholastic League will be playing: CIA Bella Vista out of Arizona, and Link Academy from Missouri. Both will play two games, including one against one another on Saturday.

articles.title: Jack Hughes scores OT game-winner as Devils outlast Red Wings in back-and-forth thriller
articles.summary: Jack Hughes scored on a breakaway off a slick pass from Jesper Bratt early in overtime, lifting the New Jersey Devils to a 5-4 win over the Detroit Red Wings...
articles.body:
DETROIT (AP) — Jack Hughes scored on a breakaway off a slick pass from Jesper Bratt early in overtime, lifting the New Jersey Devils to a 5-4 win over the Detroit Red Wings on Tuesday night.

New Jersey's Evan Rodrigues , Nico Hischier and Bratt scored tiebreaking goals and Anthony Mantha had a tying goal. Jake Allen stopped 22 shots for the Devils.

Alex DeBrincat had a pair of tying goals after Emmitt Finne and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard scored to give the Red Wings a 2-1 lead.

Detroit's John Gibson made 32 saves, including a kick save that denied Arseny Gritsyuk on an odd-man rush late in regulation to send the game to overtime.

The Red Wings got off to a rough start, getting outshot 16-0 midway through the first period. New Jersey, though, didn't take full advantage as Rodrigues scored its only goal in the opening period.

Finne scored on Detroit's third shot with 1:25 left in the first period and Brandsegg-Nygard scored on the team's next shot early in the second period.

The Devils, hoping to get back to the playoffs after finishing seventh in the division last year, acquired Rodrigues in a trade and signed Mantha — a former Red Wing — in free agency to boost their third line.

Detroit, meanwhile, had a shaky offseason.

Dylan Larkin asked to be traded and the former captain is still on the team. Simon Edvinsson , a standout defenseman, remains unsigned as a restricted free agent.

Devils forward Luke Evangelista was out with an illness after feeling worse throughout the game Monday night against Ottawa and was replaced by Stefan Noesen . New Jersey defenseman Johnathan Kovacevic made his season debut after missing all of training camp recovering from knee surgery this past spring.

Devils: Host the New York Rangers on Thursday night.

Red Wings: Host Philadelphia on Thursday night.
